fields.title: Make hook-fired writes always target the real database
fields.description: Make hook-fired writes, such as session registration, events and task status changes, always target the real database even inside a sandboxed worktree.
fields.context: After E-1426 retired companion files, the sessions table is ground truth for Claude-pane registration.
fields.analysis:
## Known limitation: deferred to E-1458 (2026-05-23)

E-1450's "all hook-fired writes go to the real DB" rule is correct for production but unconditional — it leaves no affordance for legitimate self_dev testing scenarios where a developer wants to exercise the hook binaries (the 5-10 separate Go apps per E-893 / E-1367 fan-out) against a sandbox DB without polluting the real ledger.

Implement E-1450 as designed. The current edge-case carve-outs in the prompt (test-fixture detection, sandbox-init bypass) are stand-ins, not a full solution. When hook testing against the sandbox becomes a felt need, **E-1458** ("Allow opt-in hook routing to sandbox DB for self_dev testing") addresses it properly — an opt-in mechanism (env var, per-event marker, or wrapper) that bypasses the IsSandboxActive() override at the hook entry.

Until E-1458 lands, hook tests must either inject DB handles explicitly or accept that hook events leak to the real DB.

## From the description

Fix: ALL hook-fired writes (session registration, event emission, task-status transitions) target the real DB regardless of sandbox routing,

because these reflect real-world activity not test fixture data.

Rare edge cases can be carved out individually.

Adds 'endless session start' (refuses inside Claude) plus --user-session / --new-session flags on writing verbs (also refuse inside Claude).

Synthetic well-known UUID for --user-session; fresh UUID for --new-session.

fields.title: Fix migrate-db dry run applying migrations
fields.description: Fix the migrate-db dry run so it reports pending migrations without applying them, instead of auto-migrating on open and then claiming everything was already applied.
fields.context:
cmd/endless-event main.go calls monitor.DB() to get the connection;

DB() unconditionally invokes migrate(db, MigrateOpts{Runner: RunnerAuto}) before main.go reads -dry-run.

So the real migration runs, then the dry-run code path reports everything 'already applied' — misleading no-op.

Discovered during E-1396 when a -dry-run command actually applied V11 to the real DB.
fields.analysis: Fix needs to either split DB-open from auto-migrate, plumb a dry-run signal into DB(), or deprecate the flag as a footgun.

fields.title: Fix the rebuild-required migration gate breaking fresh DBs
fields.description: Fix the gate on migrations that require a rebuild so fresh databases, such as tests and new installs, can pass it instead of being refused.
fields.context:
When a registered migration sets RequiresRebuild: true, internal/monitor/migrate.go returns ErrRequiresRebuild and refuses to advance the schema unless opts.AllowRebuild is set.

Discovered during E-1396 when adding the flag on V11 broke 53 fresh-DB tests immediately, forcing me to drop the flag and rely on BEGIN IMMEDIATE TRANSACTION alone.

The flag is currently unused on main but the next user who needs it will hit the same wall — and worse, can't ship it at all without breaking every fresh install.
fields.analysis: Fix needs an escape hatch: either auto-skip when the rebuild would be a no-op (introspect target shape), or distinguish 'fresh DB created this version' from 'existing DB needs operator approval to rebuild'.

fields.description: Add endless session status, an at-a-glance view of the session's goal task and its status, a session-state verb, and the remaining work split between you and the agent.

fields.title: Add a column recording how a task entered a session
fields.description: Add a column to session tasks recording how each task entered the session's scope: as its goal (the claimed task), surfaced (created in the session), or revisited (pre-existing).
fields.notes: Migration mechanism sequenced against E-1459, which is replacing the V-migration framework whose sequential numbering caused the V11 collision — avoid reintroducing it.
fields.context: Feeds the You/Agent split and the Goal line in session next.
fields.analysis:
Session-next accuracy finding (session 504 investigation, 2026-05-27): session_tasks records ANY task touched under a session_id, agent or human, including incidental grooming. Example: E-999/E-1064/E-1073 were recorded against session 504 because that session (the agent, acting on Mike's behalf) ran task-update on them. Accurate history, but not 'what the session worked on'. So the relation column must let session-next separate goal/surfaced/revisited work from incidental edits, and the render-side terminal-status filter (per E-1421) must drop completed/confirmed touches from the Remaining view.

Actor-identity (OPEN QUESTION -- discuss when working E-1462; not yet decided, do not pre-frame as multiple-choice): actor.id is currently built as USER@hostname (event_bridge.py emit_event, ~line 68), e.g. mikeschinkel@m4macmini.local, and is identical for agent- and human-run CLI, so the two are indistinguishable at the actor level. The current user@machine form carries useful provenance (who AND which machine) worth preserving -- do NOT collapse it to a bare 'claude'/'user'. Candidate to discuss: keep user@machine but prefix it with a role, e.g. agent:claude@m4macmini.local vs user:mikeschinkel@m4macmini.local. That distinguishes agent from human, keeps machine provenance, and generalizes to multi-user (future scope). Open sub-questions: the role vocabulary (agent/user vs claude/human), how agent context is detected (e.g. the CLAUDECODE env var Claude Code injects), and whether the role lives in actor.id or a separate actor field. Caveat: distinguishing agent from human filters human-CLI pollution but would NOT exclude E-999/1064/1073 (agent grooming, so role would be 'agent'); the relation column plus terminal-status filter are what handle incidental-vs-goal.

## From the description

Set at capture time alongside the existing auto-capture.

fields.description: Rename the --llm output flag to --agent, add --format <text|json|agent> as a long-form alias wherever an output flag exists, and add --json to task deps and task relations.
fields.notes: That is output design rather than a flag rename — detail-shaped ones belong to E-2136, list-shaped ones to E-2141, and three are pending removal decisions.
fields.analysis:
## session status: the sweep must not drop the ownership signal

Noted 2026-09-11 from E-2111's session, which hit the failure this prevents.

`session status` exposes `--json` and no text flag, so this sweep is what gives
it an agent-facing view at all. That view has a requirement the other commands
do not: **who owns each row is carried by a GLYPH, and only by a glyph.**

`classify()` in `internal/sessionstatuscmd` tests `IsFocal` before `InFlight`,
so a row renders `●` when it is this session's own task and `⟳` when a
non-focal row is in flight — meaning another session is working it. That single
character is the whole signal. The JSON already carries it structurally as
`is_focal`, `in_flight` and `relation`; the text view must carry an equivalent
in words.

WHY THIS MATTERS. A session that cannot tell its own work from another
session's reports the other session's work back to the user, who then receives
the same item twice — once here and once from the session that actually owns it.
That happened: a `/whats-left` report told Mike to confirm E-2128 and to spawn
E-1881, both of which belonged to ES-1199. The glyph was on screen and was
misread. In a text view where the glyph is simply gone, it is not misreadable,
it is unavailable.

Concretely, the agent view of a row needs enough to answer "is this mine?" —
`relation` (claimed vs surfaced) and `in_flight` at minimum. The owning session
id is NOT needed for the render: a user navigates to a session by task id, and
an agent only needs to know the row is not its own. `--json` may carry the id
even though the text view does not.

This is also the clearest evidence for `--agent` over `--plain`. Rendering
"another session is working this" where the human view prints `⟳` is not
stripping chrome; it is rendering for a reader who cannot interpret a glyph.

## From the description

Scope is the FLAG SURFACE only: rename --llm to --agent on the 12 commands carrying both flags, remove --llm rather than keeping a deprecated alias per no-legacy, add --format wherever an output flag exists, and add --json to task deps and task relations, the two commands having --llm and no --json.

Rejected --plain, which this task originally proposed on the premise that the flag merely strips chrome from human output: it does not.

task show --llm emits key=value lines with fields regrouped and relations flattened, so --plain would misname it in the opposite direction from --llm; --agent names what actually varies, the reader.

Explicitly NOT in scope: writing agent renderings for the 16 commands that have --json and no agent view.

fields.title: Fix just land failing to record self-modifying branches
fields.description: Fix just land so recording the landing runs in a fresh process after the merge, instead of failing when the landed branch changed the event bridge or config code it loads.
fields.notes:
E-1474 makes it recoverable; this task prevents it on the canonical 'just land' path.

Related E-1005 (uv editable install going stale under multi-session use) is a different uv state bug; this one fires even with a healthy editable install.
fields.context: Observed 2026-05-29 landing E-1510 (which added config.resolved_worktree_endless_go).
fields.analysis:
Recurred 2026-08-20 landing E-2011, which renamed endless.project_path.normalize
to resolved: main advanced, `_record_landing`'s lazy `from endless.event_bridge
import emit_event` loaded post-merge code against the pre-merge
endless.project_path still in sys.modules, and the land died with `cannot import
name 'resolved' from 'endless.project_path'`. No task_landings row; re-running
`just land` recorded it. Same function, same import, same mechanism as the
2026-05-29 occurrence on E-1510. Filed again as E-2013 before this task was
found; E-2013 is declined as a duplicate and carries a plan whose design is the
in-product fork this task's sibling E-1516 objects to.

Two things have changed since this was filed, and both bear on the chosen remedy.

1. It now fires on the CANONICAL path, not the bare one. The `just land` recipe
   makes a single `endless worktree land` call — E-1941 deliberately moved the
   schema-apply step OUT of the Justfile and INTO the command, so that the apply
   happens after the ff-merge. So the single-process path this task treats as
   "the canonical path fixed by Justfile orchestration" is the only path there
   is, and E-1516's stated promotion trigger ("if the bare path becomes more
   commonly used") has effectively fired.

2. The `--no-record` / `--record-only` split under-covers. It isolates Step 6
   only. Everything E-1941 and E-1799/E-1800 have since moved after the ff-merge
   runs in that same exposed process: `_apply_branch_schema_changes` (5.5),
   `_run_post_land_script`, `_check_post_land_residue`, `_reap_stale_worktrees`.
   Whichever of them imports a module for the first time after the merge is
   equally exposed, and which one that is depends on what the process happened to
   touch earlier — so the failure is order-dependent and will not reproduce.
   The loud case is an ImportError; the quiet case is a newly-imported module
   reading an already-cached module's changed constant, which raises nothing.

Consequence for the decision this task is blocked on: the Justfile-is-the-dev-only
-layer escape hatch got narrower when E-1941 moved work inward. Isolating the
whole post-merge tail — not just the recording — is what the fix has to do,
whether it is done by the recipe or inside the command.

## From the description

Fix: add --no-record flag to 'endless worktree land' (inverse of E-1479's --record-only); update the just land recipe to call 'endless worktree land --no-record E-N' then 'endless worktree land --record-only E-N'.

The second invocation is a fresh Python process — consistent imports.

Bare 'endless worktree land' (no Justfile) still has the bug along that path; a separate maybe task tracks whether to address it.

Implementation would have _land_worktree fork after ff-merge to run _record_landing in a fresh subprocess, sidestepping the import cache —

fields.title: Add a table for typed task content
fields.description: Add a task content table so a task can hold many typed content items such as outcome, notes, analysis and justification, replacing the fixed content columns.
fields.notes: Discussed in a recent session that I cannot relocate; surfaced again 2026-06-05 during epic-type design — Mike flagged it as the better long-term shape for epic narrative storage and as the storage location for type=research justification text.
fields.analysis:
Per ED-1509 (epic content-field convention): once this table exists, revisit epic content storage with purpose-specific content types instead of overloading the legacy columns — in particular a 'design' content type for an epic's design/decisions/interface-contracts (currently overloaded into 'analysis'), and possibly distinct 'vision' and 'roadmap' types. Choose types for fit-for-purpose, not by reusing the few existing columns. ED-1509's field semantics are storage-agnostic and survive this migration.


## Scope split settled 2026-09-13: ship the TABLE, defer the POLICY

The reason this has been deferred is the design space it opens: once content is
not constrained to a fixed set of columns, do content names change per task
type, and are names added or removed for specific types? That question is real
and it is large.

It is also SEPARABLE, and separating it is what makes this task shippable.

- **The table is a storage change.** Ship `task_content` carrying exactly today's
  four names with today's semantics, and behaviour is unchanged.
- **The vocabulary is a policy change.** Whether a brainstorm gets `findings`
  instead of `plan` needs no answer for the table to land.

In a row store, adding a name later is an INSERT, not a migration. That is the
entire point of the change — and it means DEFERRING this task is the expensive
option, because until it lands every new content need costs a column.

Corollary Mike raised and worth holding: this will never be one-and-done. New
content kinds get identified on an ongoing basis. So what is settled once is the
CONVENTION, not the list — one lowercase single-token name per content kind, and
the same token used by `task_content.name`, the Agent Folio Format `Name` header,
and the CLI flag. A new content kind then inherits the rule without a fresh
decision, and no mapping between vocabularies is ever needed.

## NOT blocked by E-894

An earlier framing in discussion claimed this needed a working ledger rebuild,
and therefore the Go port first. That was wrong and is withdrawn.

What this actually needs is the PROJECTOR taught to write `task_content` rows,
plus an ordinary SQLite migration moving existing column values into rows.
Rebuild is the disaster-recovery path, not the deploy path. The only true
residual is that rebuild — already broken, and on hold until after E-894 — gains
one more thing it must learn whenever it is fixed. That is not a prerequisite.

## Relationship to the agent-output work

This makes `task meta` cheaper rather than harder. `meta` reports which content
fields exist and how large they are; over columns that is computed per field,
over `task_content` it is one query returning exactly that shape.

It is also where decision content lands if E-1868 proceeds — see E-1861's
analysis for the two-homes split (`tasks.type='decision'` for architectural
decisions, a `decision` content row for implementation decisions) and for why a
decision needs parts rather than one capped description field.



## A first import for this table (noted by E-2155, 2026-09-18)

E-2155's refusal inventory is 1136 rows — one per user-facing refusal or warning
site, with its class, remedy or decision, and notes. It is committed as a TSV
under docs/ because E-2159 reads it row by row while converting, and because
nothing in Endless stores tabular research today.

That file is the exception this table removes. When task_content ships, import
those rows as typed content on E-2155 and delete the file: it is per-task,
typed, and machine-read, which is exactly the shape this table is for. Worth
checking against the schema while designing it — a 1136-row set is a useful
stress case for whether content rows are one-per-artifact or one-per-record.




## Surface words are a per-type display concern, not a second stored name

Folded down from E-1992 when that task became an epic, because the convention
this task already settled is what governs it.

The primary instruction content stays ONE stored name. The word varies only at
the surface, where agents read and write it: `--plan` on todo/bugfix/epic,
`--brief` on research, `--topic` on brainstorm, rendering under the matching
heading. `--plan` stays accepted on every task type as a universal alias, so an
agent reaching for it on a brainstorm lands in the right row instead of an
error.

Storage stays singular because the objection being answered is behavioural — an
agent resists "plan" on a brainstorm — and behaviour is driven by the flag and
the label, not by the schema. Singular storage also keeps the plan-present gate
one question with no per-type mapping behind it.

This sits with the deferred vocabulary policy above, not with the table: the
table ships carrying today's names, and nothing here has to be answered first.

## From the description

Plan to design at pickup.

fields.title: Add endless epic status command
fields.description: Add 'endless epic status <id>', a dashboard for one epic showing its state, every child's phase, status, blockers and session, and which children are actionable next.
fields.analysis:
# Design reasoning — epic status vs session status

## Decision (2026-06-29, Mike)

Chose (a) + (c): **keep `epic status`, re-scoped to not duplicate `session status`,
but defer it** (phase `later`) until a concrete coordinator need arises that
`session status` cannot meet. Surfaced while coordinating E-1537 by hand with
`epic list` / `epic show` / `task bind`.

## The two reads are a "status family" — same presentation, different anchor

`session status` / `session monitor` (the soon-to-be-renamed `session next`, E-1465)
is **session-anchored, bottom-up**: it resolves a *focal task* from the current tmux
window (live session active-task → `@endless_task_id` → most-recent live session) and
shows that task's neighborhood — parent/spawning task, siblings worked by other
sessions on the same focal, cross-session in-flight work, and the focal's direct
dependents. Its row set is driven by which sessions are live and the dependency graph
around the focal. Answers: "what's happening across the swarm around the work I'm on."

`epic status` is **epic-anchored, top-down**: given an explicit epic id, it shows the
epic's own state plus the COMPLETE roster of its children. Answers: "what's the full
state of epic E-NNN so I can decide what to spawn or unblock next."

## Why session status does NOT subsume epic status

Three structural gaps session status can't close:

1. **Targeting any epic from anywhere, no session required.** session status can only
   reach an epic if you're in a session whose focal *is* that epic. epic status takes an
   id — works from a plain shell, for an epic with zero live sessions, for an epic you're
   not currently working in. For a coordinator this is the common case, not the edge.
2. **The complete roster, including what's not moving.** session status's children come
   from live sessions + the focal's graph neighbors, so a not-started / blocked /
   session-less child can be absent. A coordinator's job is exactly seeing those — the
   "what's left."
3. **Next-actionable hint** (ready children, no open blockers) is an epic-roster
   computation, not a session-neighborhood one.

It also must earn its place against `epic show --children` (E-1540), which already prints
a static children table. epic status's differentiator over both siblings: roster +
*live* decorations (blocker / active-session per child) + actionability, targetable by id.

## Scope cut

- IN: epic's own state; complete child roster (every child) with phase, status, blocker
  indicator, active-session indicator; next-actionable hint. Reuse the decoration layer
  `session next` already computes in Go (blocked-by/blocks, active-session) — don't
  re-derive.
- OUT: cross-session in-flight / parent-spawn neighborhood (that's session status's job at
  the keyboard); full child descriptions / plan text / decision history (that's epic show
  / task show).

## Deferral

Committed but parked at `later`: build it when the coordinator need bites and session
status demonstrably can't cover it. The implementation plan is intentionally NOT written
yet — author it at pickup. Was blocked by E-1540 (the `epic` command group), now satisfied
(E-1540 assumed).

## From the description

Shows the epic's own state plus the COMPLETE child roster (every child, including not-started/blocked/session-less ones) with per-child phase, status, blocker indicator, and active-session indicator, plus a 'next actionable' hint (ready children, no open blockers). Built on the decoration layer 'session next' already computes in Go (reuse, don't re-derive).

Explicitly does NOT reproduce session status's cross-session in-flight / parent-spawn neighborhood (that's session status's job at the keyboard), nor epic show's child descriptions/plan text.

Unique value = explicit-id targeting + complete roster + actionability.

fields.analysis:
# Verification-suite system — design analysis

Per ED-1509, this epic's `analysis` holds the distilled design (vision, locked decisions,
interface contracts); the forward roadmap is in the epic's plan (`--text`); the full research is
in E-1600's `outcome`.

## Vision

A product feature of Endless: every task that reaches `verify` carries a committed, executable
**verification suite** — the complete test set (unit + end-to-end) proving that task's
acceptance criteria. Runnable three ways: (a) a bare `git clone` with Endless NOT installed;
(b) `endless verify <id>` on the user's behalf; (c) an AI agent so the user needn't run it.

## Terminology

- **verification suite** — the committed, executable proof of a task's acceptance criteria
  (unit + e2e). (Avoids "artifact," which in CI/CD means a build output.)
- **test runner** — the execution engine that runs the suite (`go test`, `pytest`, `bats`,
  testscript). Endless is never the test runner; it discovers suites, invokes the runner,
  isolates the run, normalizes results, presents pass/fail. (Avoids "runtime.")

## Load-bearing constraint

Endless must require NO external tool to use the core feature. Requiring mise/Docker/etc. would
itself be a reason not to adopt Endless. Heavier tooling must never become a precondition; the
design only must not block adding it later.

## Design principles

1. Triple-runnable (bare clone with no Endless / by Endless / by an agent).
2. Discoverer/orchestrator, never the test runner — convention + manifest, not a dependency.
3. Native runners underneath + a uniform discovery/result contract on top.
4. The suite is ALL testing for the task's scope (unit + e2e); may be slow when needed. Tiering
   = when you run (smoke vs full), not what's included.
5. CLI-only is a PRO — lets Endless drive tools invisibly.
6. All-Go future: no Python/uv lock-in.
7. Not a CI/CD platform. Hermetic builds / production parity are user-owned.
8. The chosen form must be trivially authorable by an AI agent with minimal-to-zero user input.

## Locked decisions (2026-06-20, post E-1600 research)

1. **Result contract = CTRF schema, subset implementation, vendored writer.** Implement only the
   CTRF fields we need, field-names/shapes matching CTRF, pinned to the CTRF snapshot
   (2025-11-24). Read native producers ourselves; NO runtime dependency on external CTRF
   reporters. (CTRF is pre-1.0/single-maintainer — we own the writer so upstream churn can't
   reach us; "CTRF-shaped" keeps later interop free.)
2. **Suite location = `.endless/tasks/<id>/`** — a product-controlled directory, so the
   convention is identical across every project regardless of its `tests/` layout.
3. **Scope = Stages 1–2 now; defer Stage 3 (containers) and Stage 4 (PTY/tmux).** Dogfood on
   Endless (the easy Tier-0 case) first.
4. **Build inside Endless, keep the seam clean** for possible later extraction; no extraction
   cost now beyond clean boundaries.

Note (general): the **product** Tier-0 substrate is a fresh temp working dir + isolated env
(temp `HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`) — zero-dependency and app-agnostic. The temp-SQLite "fresh task
DB" is NOT part of the product runner; it is incidental to Endless being the system-under-test
(Endless's DB lives under XDG, so XDG isolation supplies it automatically). Tier 0 fits any
project whose state is contained by a temp dir; arbitrary projects with service dependencies
default to Tier 3 (containers), selected by the suite's declared `needs`. This does not violate
principle 2 — the core never *requires* a tool; `needs` selects the substrate a suite asks for.

## Interface Contract (foundation trio E-1602/E-1603/E-1604 MUST conform)

The three foundation children define interlocking interfaces. They are pinned here so the
children cannot diverge.

### A. The verify manifest — two-level config (E-1602 landed the per-task schema)

Two layers, merged at discovery (mirrors Endless's layered config / go-cfgstore):

- **Project-level `.endless/verify.toml`** — shared `setup`, default `needs`/`format`, shared
  fixtures. (Added by the setup/config-layering follow-up task.)
- **Per-task `.endless/tasks/<id>/verify.toml`** — the `runner`, task-specific `seed`,
  overrides. Beside the suite files and an optional `fixtures/`.

Discovery: glob `.endless/tasks/*/verify.toml`; merge with the project file. TOML (comments; no
YAML coercion footguns; Go-idiomatic). Kept flat by design.

```toml
schema = 1
task   = "E-1234"

[[check]]                              # first-class runner (B): structured tests
runner = "gotest"
tests  = ["TestFoo", "TestBar"]        # → go test -run 'TestFoo|TestBar' ./...

[[check]]
runner = "pytest"
tests  = ["tests/test_x.py::test_a"]

[[check]]                              # non-first-class (A): raw command fallback
runner  = "bats"
command = "bats ./.endless/tasks/E-1234/cli.bats"
format  = "tap"

setup  = ["just build"]               # top-level: prepare the project (cmds or script refs)
tiers  = ["smoke", "full"]            # optional
seed   = ["fixtures/baseline.json"]   # optional (E-1606)
needs  = []                           # optional; selects isolation tier (Stage 3+)
```

A verification is a **list of `[[check]]` entries** (A+B hybrid). First-class runners
(`gotest`, `pytest` to start) use a structured `tests` list Endless translates to the native
filter; any other runner uses a raw `command` + declared `format` (default `tap`). Rule: `tests`
is legal only on a first-class runner; otherwise require `command`. `setup`/`seed`/`needs`/`tiers`
stay top-level. This is the meta-test/selection concept: one ticket composes checks that SELECT
across the project's own runner set (reference); a snapshot is just a copied test file run by a
`command` check. The manifest is a POINTER, not a spec — it names runners and selects tests,
never re-describes them (no Gherkin-style spec layer).

**Three precondition kinds** (do not conflate): `needs` = provision the substrate (what must
exist); `setup` = prepare the project (build/install/migrate/codegen); `seed` = load
state/fixtures. Standard script homes: `.endless/verify/` (project-shared, e.g.
`.endless/verify/setup.sh`) and each task's `.endless/tasks/<id>/` dir; short steps may inline.

### B. Runner → result dataflow (E-1603 produces, E-1604 consumes)

1. E-1603 reads the manifest and creates **generic, app-agnostic per-run isolation**: a fresh
   temp working dir + an isolated env (temp `HOME`, temp `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`) so the suite can't
   touch the developer's real home/config (Tier 0). The runner has NO application-specific state
   knowledge (no task DB, no SQLite). *Self_dev note:* since Endless's own DB lives under
   `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, isolating XDG gives an Endless-SUT suite a fresh DB for free — incidental,
   not runner logic.
2. E-1603 runs preconditions in order: provision (Tier-0 no-op) → merged `setup` steps (abort
   loudly on failure) → `seed` (E-1606).
3. For each `[[check]]`, E-1603 runs it (first-class: translate `tests` → native filter; raw:
   run `command`), capturing exit code + the native result stream named by the check's `format`.
4. E-1603 passes each (raw native stream, `format`) to E-1604's normalizer; E-1604 normalizes
   each to CTRF and **merges all checks into one report**.
5. E-1603 tears down the temp dir (honor a `--keep` debug flag).

### C. The CTRF-subset envelope (E-1604 owns — the stable output contract)

A single JSON document (UTF-8). Subset we implement now:

- Top: `results.tool.name`; `results.summary { tests, passed, failed, skipped, pending, other,
  start, stop }`; `results.tests[]`.
- Per test: required `name`, `status` (`passed|failed|skipped|pending|other`), `duration` (ms);
  optional `message`, `trace`, `suite`, `stdout`, `stderr`, `attachments[]`
  (`{ name, contentType, path }` — the non-text hook: screenshots/HTTP transcripts), `extra`.
- Field names/shapes match CTRF; emit only this subset; ignore the rest until needed. Endless
  WRITES this itself from the native stream; no external CTRF reporter at runtime.

### D. Exit-code contract (bare-clone mode)

The `runner` string alone must exit 0 on all-pass and non-zero on any failure, with no Endless
present. CTRF normalization and seeding are Endless-only enhancements unavailable in bare mode;
the runner string must be self-sufficient.

## Lessons from ad-hoc prototypes

`tests/tasks/e-1577-verify.sh` and `tests/tasks/e-1570-verify.sh` are reference-only prototypes
(not deliverables). Lessons, now folded into the design: (a) the sandbox lacked a supported
seeding verb (E-1570's author reached into `endless-go session-query record-bg-agent`) → E-1606
adds first-class seeding; (b) two happy paths were left MANUAL because they `exec` into
`claude attach` or need a live tmux → Stage 4 (deferred) automates these via PTY/disposable
container; (c) Click prints `No such option: --type` with a capital `N`, so the E-1577
prototype's lowercase `"no such option"` pattern silently false-negatives on flag-removal
checks (a "this option was removed" assertion that never actually matches) → the shared
"option rejected" assertion helper must match the runner's real output case-accurately, or
normalize case before comparing. Surfaced building `tests/tasks/e-1540-verify.sh`.

## From the description

Script is committed to version control, optionally reviewable by Mike before running, and ultimately part of repeatable testing.

Long-term: subagents/Codex generate the scripts, adversarial agents review them for coverage.

treat it as an example of shape/output to learn from, NOT a deliverable of this task.

Pickup session should INTERVIEW Mike on framework shape (output format, assertion style, DB sandbox setup, runner integration with `just test`, naming/location, how the convention propagates into spawn templates / endless guide so future sessions produce one for every verify-handoff) BEFORE planning. DO NOT plan until the interview is complete.

Load-bearing for AI authoring and the bare-clone guarantee:

Critically this includes the one-command handoff contract (added at Mike's direction, 2026-07-10): the verify-handoff step of every spawn template must direct the session to run project-wide regression itself and REPORT it in prose, and to hand the user exactly ONE verification command, never an enumerated checklist of manual test commands. Dogfooding target: run the one verify command; if it passes, we are done.

fields.notes: Stage 2:

fields.description: Investigate how verify suites report all passed while a feature is silently broken, when advisory code swallows its own failures or a stale global binary gets used.
fields.context: Surfaced while writing tests/tasks/e-1572-verify.sh.
fields.analysis: Recommends an ENDLESS_GO_BIN injection seam, a debug toggle that surfaces swallowed errors, mandatory positive controls paired with every silence assertion, and a tripwire meta-check.

fields.title: Surface swallowed advisory-code errors under a debug toggle
fields.description: Surface errors that advisory, best-effort code swallows to stderr or the log under a debug toggle, without changing control flow, and apply this to existing advisory sites.
fields.notes: Surfaced by E-1612.
fields.context: Advisory/best-effort code that swallows its own failures (e.g. _bg_throttle_warn) makes 'correctly did nothing' indistinguishable from 'silently broke', which lets verify suites report false greens.

fields.title: Fix 5 failing handoff render tests
fields.description: Fix the five failing handoff render tests: epic handoffs missing the children status breakdown, and the research variant missing its completion-with-outcome instruction.
fields.context:
independent of E-1576 (confirmed: they fail at HEAD before any E-1576 edit).

The rendered handoff text lacks the strings the tests assert.

Cluster 1 — tests/test_handoff_children_state.py (test_epic_render_shows_no_children_yet, _shows_mixed_breakdown, _shows_single_bucket, _drops_redundant_child_count_block): epic handoffs no longer carry a 'Children:' status-breakdown line.

fields.title: Reject maybe-phase parent-child relations on write
fields.description: Reject task add and update operations that would put a maybe-phase task under a parent or give a parented task the maybe phase, and add a survey of existing violations.
fields.notes: Decision recorded separately.
fields.analysis:
Atomic combo task update X --phase next --parent E-Y remains legal (promote+parent in one shot is fine).

Rationale: maybe = uncommitted; parent-child = scope binding; mixing creates phantom scope — a parent that appears done while uncommitted commitments linger inside.

Hard rejection, no --force (gates not guardrails).

Includes a one-shot survey command listing existing pre-rule violations so the owner can convert each to relates_to or leave as standalone.

fields.description: Remove the title-verb completability check when completing epic tasks, since an epic's deliverable is its outcome text rather than behavior.
fields.notes: Decision recorded separately.
fields.context: Hit concretely on E-1564: type=epic + title verb 'implement' deadlocked because the type gate requires completed but the verb gate forbids it.
fields.analysis: Epics complete via completed (per E-1537 / E-1552 outcome) and their deliverable IS the outcome text, not behavior — so the verb-as-deliverable-signal logic the gate enforces does not apply.

fields.title: Revise verify.toml to a list of checks

fields.notes: E-1602 landed a single runner/format manifest.
fields.analysis:
first-class runners (gotest, pytest) use a structured 'tests' list Endless translates to native filters; other runners use a raw 'command' + declared 'format'.

Endless runs all checks, normalizes each to CTRF, merges into one report, and emits resolved commands for bare-clone.

fields.title: Restore status row task and epic after /bg and attach
fields.description: Restore the endless tmux status row showing the task and epic after a Claude session is backgrounded with /bg and later reattached with claude attach.
fields.context: Status row is the at-a-glance task-awareness surface the coordinator workflow depends on; silent regression makes bg-dispatch unsafe for long-running coordinator sessions.
fields.analysis:
Investigation first step: tmux show -g before/after /bg, and again after claude attach, to isolate which transition clears status-format[N].

Likely fix: a hook on attach (SessionStart? PaneAttach if it exists?) that re-runs endless tmux apply.

fields.title: Show task and parent ids in background agent labels
fields.description: Show the task id, and the parent epic id for an epic's child, in background agent labels in Agent View, e.g. '<parent_id>/<task_id>: <description>'.
fields.context:
Agent View currently shows bg agent rows with a generic title derived from the handoff's first prose line, no task ID prefix.

With this in place the global Agent View becomes scannable and partially mitigates the lack of native epic-scoped filtering.
fields.analysis:
Three label shapes by task type: (1) standalone task → '<task_id>: <description>'; (2) epic task → '<epic_id>: <description>'; (3) child of an epic → '<parent_id>/<task_id>: <description>'.

Likely changes: revise --name argument to claude --bg AND restructure the handoff's opening line so Claude's own title-inference picks up the ID prefix (Agent View may render either or both).

fields.title: Add endless agents command listing active-epic bg agents

fields.notes:
Pairs with E-1620's richer labels — Agent View is global, this is the epic-scoped supplement.

TUI version filed as the 'later' task; this one is the plain-text now-task.
fields.context: Mid-term substitute for native Agent View filtering, which Claude Code does not provide.
fields.analysis:
that queries sessions WHERE kind_id=(SELECT id FROM session_kinds WHERE slug='background') AND state='working' AND active_epic_id=<resolved-epic>, prints id/short_id/task/title/started_at.

--epic E-NNNN overrides the auto-resolved epic; --all drops the epic filter entirely (effectively the same as claude agents but endless-side).

fields.title: Build TUI monitor of per-epic bg agent sessions

fields.description: Fix duplicate session rows created on each Claude launch with no tmux pane by deduplicating on the session's active task when the pane is empty.
fields.context:
Tasks accrue many sessions rows because the dedup key is session_id (Claude UUID), not active_task_id, and the only dedup path (collision-invalidation by tmux pane) is inert when TMUX_PANE is empty.

Each launch INSERTs a fresh-UUID ghost row.

fields.title: Remove ghost session rows via the event layer
fields.description: Remove the accumulated sub-10-second ghost session rows through the event layer rather than a raw SQL delete, checking references from other tables first.
fields.context: (37 under strict criteria: ended, kind_id=1, <10s, no session_statuses, not newest-per-task; ~298 under loose filter).
fields.analysis:
Must NOT be a raw endless sql --write DELETE: sessions(id) is FK-referenced by 7 tables (session_messages, focuses, task_landings, decisions, session_gates, project_next_*), and per E-807/E-808 the event log is authoritative so a projection rebuild would resurrect deleted rows.

Prune at the ledger/compensating-event layer and check FK refs first.

fields.title: Improve session end to close rows on idle timeout
fields.description: Improve session ending to close sessions at last activity plus an idle timeout, so end times and durations reflect real session life rather than a later sweep.
fields.context:
Pattern-B: SessionEnd/EndSession (claude.go) rarely fires (harness is killed, not cleanly exited), so sessions linger state='working' until a later reaper / collision sweep marks a batch 'ended' at one shared instant (e.g. 6 rows all ending 2026-05-27T02:13:07).

Effect: last_activity is bumped far past real life, durations span days, and duration becomes useless as a 'real session' signal.

fields.title: Explore guarding against alt-worktree proliferation
fields.description: Explore whether to discourage or forbid extra worktrees per task, modeling multi-checkout needs as child tasks instead, what breaks if we do, and how respawn is affected.
fields.context:
Today a task can spawn additional worktrees at .endless/worktrees/e-<id>-<slug>/.

Mike wants to guard toward one-worktree-per-task and instead model legitimate multi-checkout needs (A/B implementations, run-while-edit, bisect/snapshot-compare) as CHILD TASKS of the core task, each with its own plan, plus a compare/pick task.
fields.analysis: Policy/research task -- outcome is a recommendation.

fields.title: Build respawn to reopen a resolved task in its worktree
fields.description: Build respawn to reopen a resolved task or session into its worktree and sandbox, rebuilt if reaped, handing off by asking the user's goal and refusing when a session is live.
fields.notes: See children for the split.
fields.analysis:
Driven by discoverability: respawn is an alias surface over a revised spawn --reopen.

Liveness-guarded (refuse if a session is already live; navigate to it instead).

fields.title: Revise task spawn --reopen
fields.description: Revise task spawn --reopen to refuse when a session is already live, reuse or rebuild the task's worktree and sandbox database, and inherit the most applicable prior session.
fields.analysis: (1) liveness-guard -- if a session is already live for the task, do NOT spawn; foreground -> tmux switch-client to its pane, bg -> point at task attach; (2) ensure/rebuild the worktree -- reuse if present, else fresh branch off main (reaped-by-land/drop both fine), and recreate the self-dev sandbox DB; (3) inherit the most-applicable prior ended session by default (live-first, else newest with dur>=10s OR populated process/transcript_path; skip sub-10s ghosts; never pick by max duration -- Pattern B poisons it); --new-session opts into a fresh session row + fresh worktree.

fields.title: Add task respawn and session respawn entry points
fields.description: Add task respawn as an alias for task spawn --reopen, and session respawn that reopens by session id or by task, both refusing when a session is already live.
fields.analysis:
session respawn <id> resolves session -> (task, that session's worktree) and runs the reopen core anchored via --worktree; session respawn --task E-NNN resolves to the most-applicable session for the task (same live-first / skip-ghost rule).

Both refuse when a session is already live for the task (navigate to it).

Foreground + --bg parity with spawn.

fields.description: Add a single type-agnostic respawn handoff template that points at the worktree, gives the prior outcome and status as context, and tells the agent to ask the user's goal first.
fields.analysis:
It: (1) leads with /cd <abs worktree path>; (2) states the restore case (reused vs rebuilt-off-main) and carries prior outcome + last session_statuses snapshot as read-only context; (3) instructs: this was previously worked/landed -- ASK the user their goal for reopening before doing anything, then run endless guide.

Revisit per-type variants later if too blunt.

fields.title: Add a submitted status and approve gate
fields.description: Add a 'submitted' status between unplanned and ready, with an agent 'submit' verb and a user-only 'approve' verb, so 'ready' means approved rather than merely planned.
fields.context: Plan-attach auto-promotes unplanned->ready, so 'ready' means 'agent drafted a plan', not 'Mike approved it' - Mike can't tell reviewed from unreviewed and a background loop can't trust 'ready'.
fields.analysis:
'submitted' = spec-complete, awaiting approval; agent-settable two ways: a plan was attached OR the description alone is a sufficient spec (plan-vs-no-plan carried by tasks.text, not status).

This makes unplanned-vs-submitted the spawn-readiness signal (unplanned = needs a plan; submitted = spawnable-from-description, pending approval), so the agent proactively signals which instead of Mike asking.

Remove auto-promote; add submit (agent) + approve (Mike) verbs; forbid kind=background sessions from approve and from non-ready pickup.

fields.title: Show inherited task and epic in status row for /bg sessions
fields.description: Show the right task and epic in the tmux status row for Claude sessions backgrounded with /bg and reattached, by binding the pane to the background session and inheriting from its parent.
fields.notes: Full diagnosis + design in E-1619 text.
fields.context: A /bg'd Claude session runs under the Claude daemon with no $TMUX_PANE and a new session id, so endless can't map it to the viewing pane or carry its task/epic across — the status row blanks and never recovers.
fields.analysis: (P1) wrap 'claude attach' to call a new 'endless session bind --session <id> --process $TMUX_PANE' verb so the pane resolves to the bg session; (P2) on the bg child's SessionStart, find the parent via shared transcript message uuids in session_messages and inherit its active_task_id/active_epic_id.

fields.title: Diagnose status row vanishing on /bg and claude attach
fields.description: Diagnose which transition clears the endless tmux status row when a Claude session is backgrounded with /bg and reattached, and the underlying mechanism.
fields.notes:
## Justification

Diagnosis required multi-layer investigation (tmux option scoping, process-env probing of Claude's bg daemon, job-dir/transcript inspection, DB session analysis) whose findings stand on their own and feed the bug's fix plan; too substantial to inline in the bug's do-text.

## From the description

Investigation child of the E-1619 bug:
fields.analysis: Approach in text; diagnosis in outcome.

fields.title: Research migrations and rebuild-db event upcasting
fields.description: Research forward schema and value migrations and replay-time event upcasting, so rebuilding the database can transform historical events without rewriting committed ledger files.
fields.notes:
## Justification

Designing event-upcasting + a reinstated migration framework spans the projector, ledger format, event versioning, and schema-change pipeline — substantial architecture that must be researched/designed before implementation. Mike explicitly requested it as a parallel research effort triggered by the E-1252 half-rename incident.

## From the description

Migration framework was removed earlier (too slow pre-product).
fields.context: E-1252's status rename exposed the cost: renaming a stored value forced rewriting the committed ledger, because rebuild-db replays raw event payloads.
fields.analysis:
Deliverable: recommended design + options/tradeoffs to plan an implementation epic.

Research only.

fields.title: Fix tasks stranded on old status slugs after a rename
fields.description: Fix about 439 tasks still holding status slugs from before the status vocabulary rename by updating the live database and the ledger to the new slugs.
fields.context: 343 needs_plan, 20 in_progress, 76 verify rows still hold old slugs the new code doesn't recognize, so task active/filters break for ~439 tasks.
fields.analysis:
Fix DIRECTLY on the live DB (a .sql change-file UPDATE via apply-change) + rewrite the ledger payload.status values for consistency; do NOT use rebuild-db (its replay is lossy, drops ~233/947 tasks).

Also add the missing 'unapproved' status to the valid set.

fields.title: Guard rebuild-db --confirm against a lossy projection
fields.description: Guard rebuild-db --confirm by refusing, or requiring a second force, when the rebuilt task count is well below the live count, and report the failed inserts.
fields.notes: the faithful-replay cure is the research task E-1652.
fields.context:
rebuild-db --confirm replaces the tasks table with a from-scratch ledger projection that currently replays to only ~714 tasks vs 947 live (FK-before-parent, duplicate tasks.id, invalid phase).

It would silently destroy ~25% of tasks; only dry-run-by-default has prevented a wipe.
fields.analysis: Guardrail only;

fields.title: Collapse worktree and sandbox naming to canonical e-<id>
fields.description: Collapse worktree and sandbox handling to recognize only the canonical e-<id> names, dropping support for alternate slugged variants, so each task has exactly one worktree.
fields.notes:
Implements the E-1643 recommendation (decision ED-1515):

Full touch-point list in E-1643's outcome.
fields.context: Precondition confirmed: no e-<id>-slug dirs exist.
fields.analysis:
Drop the e-<id>-* glob and lexicographic-first pick in WorktreePathForTask (internal/monitor/worktree.go); drop the optional -slug from the path regexes (_WORKTREE_TASK_ID_RE in src/endless/worktree_cmd.py, TaskIDFromWorktreePath in internal/monitor/worktree_lock.go); collapse sandbox naming in src/endless/config.py; tidy now-moot slug comments (reap_worktrees.go, db.go); update CLAUDE.md and 'endless guide orchestration' to document the child-task model for multi-checkout needs; update any slug-tolerance tests.

No active block on raw 'git worktree add' -- a non-canonical dir simply stops being recognized as the task's worktree.

No migration.

Anchors by symbol, not line number (they drift).

fields.title: Research a task lint pass for mistyped or mislinked tasks
fields.description: Research an endless task lint pass that flags tasks with the wrong type or wrong links.

fields.title: Add brainstorm task type for requester-led ideation
fields.description: Add a brainstorm task type, a sibling of research, where the agent interviews the requester to draw ideas out rather than researching, then ends with a synthesis and follow-ups.
fields.context: research pulls information IN from external sources (agent-led); brainstorm draws it OUT of the requester (requester-led, interview-mode). Same information-shaped artifact, opposite flow.
fields.analysis:
The type's value is the behavioral contract it attaches: open by interviewing the requester, do not autonomously research, capture ideas, conclude with synthesis + spawned follow-ups.

Ungated (frictionless).

Includes DB enum, Go type enum, CLI --type, guide section, and spawn-handoff interview-mode branch.

fields.title: Gate task type against verb category
fields.description: Gate task creation on the title verb's category (action or investigation) being one the task type accepts, replacing the verb's completable flag.
fields.analysis:
Schema: each verb gets 'category' (usually one of action|investigation; allow a short multi-set for genuine duals like 'compare'). Each task type declares 'accepts: [categories]' (task/bug/chore -> [action]; research/brainstorm -> [investigation]). Validity(verb,type) = type.accepts contains verb.category. GATE at task creation: block on mismatch; prefer giving a dual verb BOTH categories over a justification bypass (bypasses get taken). Touch-points: src/endless/matchers.py (defaults + is_completable_verb -> category lookup), .endless/verbs.jsonl, cli.py (current completable check), wherever task types are defined (locate first), and 'endless verb' (set/show category). NOTE completable's current VALUES are correct (knowledge-type verbs whose tasks reach 'completed') -- this generalizes, not corrects. The --justification requirement on --type research is a separate per-type policy, out of scope. COORDINATION: a 'brainstorm' type + its accepts entry are being added in a parallel session touching the same type registry; sequence edits to avoid collision.

## From the description

Decouples verbs from types (scales O(verbs)+O(types) instead of O(verbs x types)); generalizes completable now that multiple types (research, brainstorm) reach 'completed'.

Design in analysis.

fields.title: Rename task types 'task' to 'todo' and 'bug' to 'bugfix'
fields.description: Rename the task type value 'task' to 'todo' and 'bug' to 'bugfix', with historical ledger events upcast so they still replay on rebuild.
fields.notes: Needs the rebuild-db upcasting pipeline so historical rows replay -- see analysis for touch-points, dependency, and coordination.

fields.title: Fix just land recording the landing with a stale binary
fields.description: Fix just land so its record-landing step uses the worktree's endless-go binary, not the stale global one, so landing a schema change that adds an enum value no longer fails integrity checks.
fields.notes: Manual recovery this time: just install && just land E-1657.
fields.context: Latent for every future mirrored-enum addition.
fields.analysis: The prior apply-change step already avoids this by using the worktree binary (PATH=$wt/bin); record-landing should too.

fields.title: Make the Claude hook block on integrity and DB failures
fields.description: Make the Claude hook exit with the blocking code on integrity and database failures, so the failure reaches the agent's context and the agent halts instead of only the user seeing it.
fields.context: So agents cannot honor 'STOP on errors' for hook/DB failures -- they never see them.
fields.analysis:
Touch-points: internal/hookcmd/claude.go ('hook claude' exit path -- make integrity/DB-open failures exit 2, not the current non-blocking code); internal/monitor/db.go Open()/VerifyIntegrity error propagation. Confirm Claude Code semantics first (PostToolUse exit 2 -> stderr fed to model AND tool flagged; other non-zero -> 'non-blocking status code', user-only). Verify (per-task script): force a task_types drift in a temp DB and assert the hook process exits 2 with the integrity message on stderr. Incident that surfaced this: brainstorm task-type landing caused a stale-binary integrity skew whose errors were invisible to the agent.

## From the description

DECIDED (Mike): ALWAYS block on integrity failure -- exit 2 from the hook so the agent halts; NO grace window for transient cross-session migration windows (a hard stop while a schema settles is correct and avoids hard-to-unravel ripple effects).

Touch-points in analysis.

fields.title: Build self-dev worktrees on claim and spawn
fields.description: Build the worktree binaries and install the hook override when task claim or spawn creates a self-dev worktree, so the hook and sandbox CLI run the worktree's candidate build instead of the global one.
fields.context:
Result: the PostToolUse hook and sandbox CLI fall back to the GLOBAL/main-checkout binary instead of the worktree's candidate build -- defeating the per-worktree sandbox's purpose of exercising candidate code (E-1281/E-998).

Observed in worktree e-1643: bin-sandbox/ present, bin/ absent, settings.json has XDG but no hook block and no PATH-prepend.

This is also what left e-1643 exposed to the stale-global-binary integrity skew.
fields.analysis:
Current auto-provision (_maybe_auto_sandbox_bind, worktree_cmd.py) already invokes 'endless-go sandbox init/bind' -- PRODUCT-compliant, NOT just; extend that pattern. Gap: it never builds the worktree binaries (no bin/) nor installs the hook override, so hook + CLI run the global binary. PRODUCT: invoke a project-declared provision script, never 'just' from shipped code. Coordinate with E-1368 (replaces bin-sandbox wrappers with binary self-detect) so this doesn't entrench bin-sandbox. Touch-points: _maybe_auto_sandbox_bind, the 'endless-go sandbox' subcommands, .endless/config.json (declare provision script), task_cmd.py claim/spawn.

## From the description

Touch-points in analysis.

fields.title: Require --outcome by task type, not by completed status
fields.description: Require --outcome when completing a research or brainstorm task, keyed on task type rather than the completed status, and correct the guide's claim about when outcome is required.
fields.context: Outcome-required is currently coupled to the 'completed' STATUS (_require_outcome_for_completed, E-1240).
fields.analysis: Epics self-complete via derivation so never require it; decline keeps its own reason rule (ED-1022, unchanged); confirm/assume never required it.

fields.title: Make just land always pick the worktree endless-go binary
fields.description: Make just land select the worktree-built endless-go binary in the land code itself for every step, rather than relying on each Justfile shellout being pointed at it.
fields.notes: E-1660 fixed just land tripping the task_types integrity gate by PATH-prepending the worktree bin to the land call,
fields.context: but binary selection is still a fragile property of the Justfile recipe: each endless-go shellout must individually be pointed at the worktree binary via PATH, and the next one added can silently forget again.
fields.analysis:
_resolve_endless_go() (or land_worktree) should prefer the worktree-built endless-go during a land regardless of --db, since the worktree binary's embedded schema always matches the rows apply-change just inserted.

Belt and suspenders: move the apply-change loop out of the Justfile into endless worktree land itself so apply-schema then advance-main then record-landing is one command that always uses the right binary internally, leaving just land a thin build+call+rebuild wrapper.

fields.title: Design a safe way to exercise event emit by hand
fields.description: Design a safe-by-construction way to run event emit by hand, such as a dry run, so a rejected mutation never leaves a stray event in the ledger.
fields.context:
Surfaced while reproducing E-1660:

Today the only safe way to exercise the integrity/projection path is to point --project-root at a throwaway git repo (what e-1660-verify.sh does), which is a convention I can forget.
fields.analysis:
Brainstorm a safe-by-construction option: e.g. an emit --dry-run / a standalone 'validate this binary's enum against this DB' mode that opens the DB and runs VerifyIntegrity WITHOUT touching the ledger, so direct invocation physically cannot pollute real state during testing.

Explore what the right primitive is (dry-run flag vs separate verb vs read-only DB open) and how it composes with the existing --db main|sandbox routing.

fields.title: Stop self-dev worktrees silently running the wrong code
fields.description: Stop Endless self-dev worktrees from silently falling back to the global install, so each reliably exercises its own candidate build for database routing, binaries, hooks and landing.
fields.notes: Groups the open tasks in this area so they stop floating as loosely-related independents.

fields.title: Require explicit database context and name it in reads
fields.description: Require an explicit database context instead of guessing one, and make every read state which database and project it answered from.
fields.context: E-1368's cwd self-detect satisfies the E-1429 gate, so the loud refusal that protected against running a non-worktree endless-go build (e.g. the global one) against a worktree's sandbox went silent — restore it.
fields.analysis:
Widened 2026-09-12 to absorb E-2132 (obsolete, replaced_by this). Owner's call: one task, not two — ED-1550 rule 3.

== HALF 1: stop the guess (this task's original scope) ==

E-1368's cwd self-detect satisfies the E-1429 gate. dbContextExplicit() is 'dbContextDir != "" || dbPathOverride != ""', and cmd/endless-go/main.go calls monitor.SelfDetectWorktreeSandbox() for every subcommand at startup, which sets dbContextDir from CWD. So a guessed context satisfies a gate whose own doc comment says only a flag or ForceRealDB counts.

The sibling comment on dbContextDir forbids exactly this for XDG_CONFIG_HOME: 'an env var can be exported once and silently route every later command to the wrong DB -- the exact failure mode the gate exists to kill'. CWD does the same thing without even an export.

The distinction is already modelled and simply never consulted: dbContextFromFlag separates an explicit flag from a cwd-detected sandbox, and SelfDetectWorktreeSandbox deliberately calls setDetectedContextDir rather than SetDBContextDir so it will not suppress the hook/tmux main pin. The principle to encode: detection decides WHERE TO LOOK; only a flag decides THAT YOU MAY OPEN IT. Config and log routing can stay CWD-derived without granting permission to read or write rows.

Python already refuses without --db inside a self-dev worktree (E-1429 gated it at both layers); it is the Go backstop that was defeated, which is why the damage surfaces only on direct endless-go invocations.

== HALF 2: state the answer (absorbed from E-2132) ==

Owner decisions, 2026-09-11/12:
  1. Announce ALWAYS, not only when the scope was inferred — for the DATABASE, in a self-dev project.
  2. Machine formats carry it as a FIELD IN THE PAYLOAD, not on stderr.
  3. Exempt contexts PINNED IN CODE (hook ForceRealDB; tmux, session-status, project-status PinMainDB). If the caller could not have influenced the choice there is nothing to disambiguate, and the tmux status line has no room for it.
  4. endless-go takes --db main|sandbox; --config-dir retires, with a --db-dir escape for callers that must name a directory without owning the process environment.
  5. WRITES announce as well as reads. E-1429's founding incident was a write — a test 'endless task add' that landed in the real ledger as E-1425 — and a write to the wrong database is the damaging case, where a wrong read only misleads.
  6. Downstream (non-self-dev), where --db does not exist and the PROJECT is the only half that reaches the user: announce the project ONLY when it is not the one enclosing cwd. With one database and usually one project, always-on is repetition.

Decisions 1, 5 and 6 are one rule, and the plan states it as one: ANNOUNCE WHAT THE INVOCATION RESOLVED, WHEN IT COULD HAVE RESOLVED OTHERWISE. In self-dev the database always could have; downstream the project only sometimes could; a pin never could.

Decision 2 departs from rowcap.echo_footer's precedent, which sends the omission trace to stderr for --json/--tsv so '| jq' will not choke. The departure is deliberate: that footer is prose COMMENTARY ABOUT an answer and would corrupt a payload, whereas the store a result came from is DATA ABOUT THE RESULT and belongs in it.

Why stderr lost, from the agent's own account of the incident below: in that session it wrote 2>/dev/null, 2>&1 | head, | tail -5 and 2>&1 | python3 -c repeatedly, each of which discards stderr or buries it under a truncation. Ranked by what actually reaches an agent: (1) a field in the structure it parses, near-unmissable because it destructures it; (2) stdout it quotes back, high, because what is in the pasted text is in the claim it makes; (3) stderr, moderate, and hardest to see when the command SUCCEEDED and returned the wanted data; (4) documentation read at session start, near zero at the moment of error. Hook stderr is weaker still — it arrives as system-reminder text an agent is told to treat as background.

== THE INCIDENT THAT RE-FOUND THIS ==

A session working E-2105 ran 'endless-go session-query list-live --project-root <main checkout>' from inside its worktree, using MAIN's binary — precisely the foreign-binary case this task was filed for. --project-root named the main checkout; the binary silently answered from the worktree sandbox, returning 2 rows where main holds 59. The session reported it to the owner as a probable product defect, having also unset XDG_CONFIG_HOME in the belief that this was what selected the sandbox. It then ran the same command against two different binaries, got identical output, and read the agreement as corroboration — a sound control for 'did my change alter this?' and none at all for 'is this number right?'. The refusal this task exists to restore would have ended it at the first command.

## From the description

endless-go gains --db main|sandbox and retires --config-dir, so one vocabulary serves both layers as the port moves to Go.

fields.title: Provision self-dev worktrees so the hook runs candidate code
fields.description: Provision each self-dev worktree at creation with its own endless-go in bin/ and point its Claude hook at it, so the hook runs candidate code instead of main's build.
fields.context: In a self_dev worktree the Claude hook silently runs main's endless-go build: claim/spawn auto-wires DB routing (sandbox bind's XDG env block) but not hook-code routing, so the session never dogfoods candidate hook/gate/session logic.
fields.analysis:
at creation, copy the installed endless-go into <worktree>/bin/ (valid immediately since it matches the worktree's main-equal code; 'just build' overwrites it in place later) and repoint the hook in <worktree>/.claude/settings.json at it — porting the claude-settings-init (E-998) logic into code so the claim/spawn verb need not shell out to just.

Scope: hook only; tmux/channel stay on main's build (shared infra, tested deliberately); the bare-shell foreign-build case is the separate E-1668.

fields.title: Add a pub-sub handler layer for lifecycle events
fields.description: Add a subscriber layer so registered handlers run actions when lifecycle events are emitted, such as bootstrapping on worktree creation or notifying on task confirmation.
fields.notes:
Builds on E-1391's worktree.created/destroyed event kinds.

Distinct from E-986, which is a single hardcoded hook point at worktree creation; this is general event-driven reaction across all event kinds.
fields.context: endless emits lifecycle events (event_bridge.emit_event → the JSONL/DB ledger) but nothing consumes them to DO anything — emission is fire-and-forget into storage.
fields.analysis: Dispatch can be in-process at emit time or a tailer over the event log.

fields.description: Build an event-upcasting pipeline that lets rebuild-db replay historical events into the current schema without rewriting the committed ledger.
fields.analysis: a std-lib Go package of forward-only declarative Cambria-style transforms + a host-registered custom escape hatch; named+content-hash migration identity grouped as manifests-of-references; the project/machine-user two-ledger scope split enforced at emit; rebuild-as-migration wiring (structural destination first, then replay); coverage linter + per-prompt tripwire; rebuild trigger on land/pull that adds a migration; golden-fixture tests for custom transforms.

fields.title: Build the forward-only upcasting transform package
fields.description: Build a standard-library-only Go package that upcasts project events to their current shape using forward-only declarative transforms plus a registered custom escape hatch.
fields.notes: Brief: E-1666 Part II.
fields.analysis:
Forward-only declarative ops (rename/add/remove/hoist/plunge/wrap/head/in/map/convert) + host-registered custom escape hatch (slice return for N to M).

Named+content-hash migration identity as manifest-of-references; events carry the applied-migration set; linear per-kind chain walk; integrity gates (hash mismatch / unregistered custom / missing referenced entry = hard error).

Ships with the golden-fixture CI harness for custom transforms (ADR-001).

No SQLite/CLI/ledger-IO.

fields.title: Split events into project and machine-user ledgers
fields.description: Split events into project and machine-user scopes declared per event kind and enforced at emit, writing project events to the committed ledger and machine-user events to a gitignored local one.
fields.notes: Brief: E-1666 Part II section 3.
fields.analysis:
Undeclared scope = hard error.

Reclassify session_status.* and focus.* as machine-user, eliminating today's muddy bucket (committed-but-not-replayed).

fields.title: Wire the upcasting package into rebuild-db
fields.description: Wire the upcasting package into rebuild-db so project events replay through the transforms into the current schema, replacing only project tables and leaving machine-user tables untouched.
fields.notes: Brief: E-1666 Part II sections 2 and 4.
fields.analysis: build the structural destination first (schema.sql + internal/schema/changes), then replay project-scope events through the transform pipeline into it, swapping only project-scope tables and leaving live machine-user tables untouched.

fields.title: Add a coverage linter and per-prompt tripwire for transforms
fields.description: Add a land-time linter checking that migrations cover every event kind they affect, and a cheap per-prompt check in the hook for registry and ledger integrity.
fields.notes: Brief: E-1666 Part II section 9.
fields.analysis:
every kind in a migration's covers list has a hash-matching entry; flag any kind carrying the affected field that is not covered; semantic-collision and structural-pairing checks.

applied-set subset of registry, no machine-user kind in the committed ledger, row-count sanity, registry integrity.

fields.description: Trigger the project rebuild when a land, rebase or pull brings in a new migration, as part of the existing land step, and fail hard when an existing migration's hash changes.
fields.notes: Brief: E-1666 Part II section 10.
fields.analysis: A changed hash on an existing migration is a hard error (history was edited), not a silent rebuild.

fields.title: Replace inline decision-replay shims with seed migrations
fields.description: Replace the ad-hoc legacy decision-replay shims in the projector with seed migrations in the upcasting pipeline, proving the pipeline covers real cases.
fields.notes: Brief: E-1666 Part II section 6.

fields.title: Build go-cambria, a forward-only Cambria-lens JSON library
fields.description: Build a reusable, forward-only Go library that applies Cambria-style schema lenses, defined as data, to JSON documents to translate them between schema versions.
fields.notes: first consumer is the Endless upcasting layer (E-1672).
fields.context: No Go implementation of Cambria exists today (TS original + a Rust port), so this has value beyond Endless.

fields.title: Add project-configurable handling for build-generated files
fields.description: Add a way for a project to declare how its build-generated tracked files are handled during land and build, so post-merge rebuilds need one-time configuration instead of recurring manual commits.
fields.context: Any project with a build system that writes tracked files (tailwind/output.css, templ, codegen, JS bundlers) dirties the worktree when 'worktree land' rebuilds post-merge, which blocks the land or forces recurring manual 'regenerate' commits (output.css hit this 3x in one week).

fields.title: Route bare endless/endless-go to the worktree build
fields.description: Route bare endless and endless-go invocations to the worktree's candidate build by detecting a self-dev worktree from the cwd and re-executing, instead of silently running main's code.
fields.notes: decisions and rationale were brainstormed in E-1687.
fields.context: From a bare (non-Claude) tmux pane inside a self-dev worktree, 'endless' (Python) and bare 'endless-go' silently run MAIN's code, so worktree changes cannot be exercised without PYTHONPATH=src or ./bin/endless-go, and new worktree flags error with 'No such option' until landed.
fields.analysis:
Absorbed E-1039 (worktree-local binary preference) on 2026-08-21 via E-1944. E-1039 carried three findings worth keeping.

CURRENT STATE, verified against main. The only installed symlink is endless-go, pointing into the MAIN checkout's bin/. E-1039's original text was written against endless-event, which no longer exists -- E-1367 consolidated the endless-* binaries into a single endless-go with subcommands. Its original premise, 'just install from worktree A makes every command hit A's binary', is also dead: CLAUDE.md now requires just install from the main checkout only, so the symlink deliberately points at main.

SCOPE OF THE GAP. The worktree binary is already preferred where it was wired explicitly: E-998 writes an absolute path to the worktree's bin/endless-go into its own .claude/settings.json, so hooks run candidate code, and ./bin/endless-go directly obviously does. What remains is NAME-RESOLVED invocation -- the Python CLI dispatching to the Go binary, and anything found via PATH -- which still reaches main's binary from inside a worktree.

RAISED IMPORTANCE. Under ED-1567 and ED-1570 the running binary determines which schema version is expected, and a mismatch HALTS rather than merely behaving stalely. A worktree sandbox DB migrated by candidate code, then opened by main's binary through the Python CLI, is a hard stop. That is why this blocks E-2020. E-894 (moving task display reads to Go) routes more commands through this path and so widens the exposure, but is not the cause.

Alternative approaches carried over from E-1039: (a) prepend ./bin to PATH in shell-init when in a worktree, (b) per-worktree install to alternative paths. The chosen approach remains the cwd self-re-exec above.

GOVERNED BY E-1972 (2026-08-21). E-1972 is the correct policy going forward and this task is subordinate to it. E-1704 as originally specified self-re-execs INTO the worktree candidate; E-1972 inverts that -- always invoke main's known-good binary, delegating to the worktree's only when that binary is VERIFIED COMPATIBLE -- because a stale pinned binary aborts before SessionStart and the window runs untracked (measured: 135 worktrees, 89 pinned to their own binary, all 103 existing worktree binaries older than main's). Do not implement the self-re-exec direction until E-1972 settles. ED-1570 supplies the compatibility test E-1972 needs: verified compatible means the binary's schema version matches the database's exactly.

## From the description

Approach is a gated, loop-guarded pre-parse self-re-exec reusing the existing worktree-path predicates;

fields.title: Pass the spawn prompt as a CLI argument and drop plan mode
fields.description: Pass the handoff to Claude as its command-line prompt when task spawn launches it, instead of typing it via tmux, and drop the forced plan-mode injection.
fields.analysis:
# Analysis — decisions and rationale

## Why the delivery mechanism is a launcher-as-window-command, not send-keys

The original ask (from a Claude Web draft) was "pass the prompt as claude's
positional arg instead of typing it." But the deeper goal is to eliminate
`send-keys` entirely: keystroke injection is fragile (a tmux prefix keystroke
arriving mid-spawn corrupts the input) and is a footgun for the planned
multiplexer-driver refactor (Herdr / a built-in multiplexer). So Claude is
launched as the tmux window's *command*, not typed into a bare shell.

## Why an endless-go subcommand owns the launch

Making `endless-go` the interface (rather than a shell script, or Python driving
tmux directly) is the multiplexer seam: the tmux specifics live behind one Go
command and can be swapped for another backend later. Internally it may still
shell out to `tmux`; the point is the interface, not the current implementation.

## Why the launcher must set the @endless_* window options (ordering)

SessionStart's spawn-bind reads `@endless_spawned_by` / `@endless_task_id` from
the tmux window (`internal/hookcmd/claude.go`). If Claude is the window's launch
command it boots immediately and races any option-setting done afterward. Having
the launcher set the options in-process *before* `exec claude` makes the ordering
deterministic and removes the old `sleep(5)`/`sleep(1)` timing heuristics. (The
cwd-based bind fallback, E-1700, still exists as a backstop but is no longer the
happy path.)

## Why parameters travel in a launch-spec file (not tmux `-e`)

`tmux new-window` runs its command through a shell, so parameters with spaces or
special chars (notably the task title in `--name`) would need shell-quoting if
passed as flags. `tmux new-window -e VAR=value` avoids that quoting, but every
such var is inherited by Claude and all its hooks/subprocesses for the whole
session — leaking transient values like the handoff path into the session
environment, where they can be mistaken for real signals. So instead the outer
`endless-go spawn-window` writes one JSON launch-spec file and the window command
is just `endless-go spawn-launch --spec <path>`: a single shell-safe path arg, no
quoting, no env leak. The handoff *text* never touches a command line either (the
launcher reads it from its file). The launcher deletes both files after reading.
(Mike, this session — chose the spec file over `-e`.)

## Confirmed decisions

- Fold into E-1705 (expand scope) rather than file a second task: the delivery
  change and the `/plan` removal edit the same ~60 lines of `spawn_plan`, and
  positional-prompt delivery inherently removes the interactive turn `/plan` was
  typed into — so they are one change. (Mike, this session.)
- Default `--permission-mode auto` for ALL spawns, including Endless self-dev:
  worktree isolation + sandbox DB make auto-accept low-risk. Making the mode
  configurable / flag-settable is wanted for the product; a `--permission-mode`
  flag is added now, defaulting to `auto`. (Mike, this session.)
- Launcher implemented as an `endless-go` subcommand even though it currently
  shells to tmux, so the multiplexer dependency is encapsulated. (Mike, this
  session.)

## Known risk / open verification

Claude Code's docs confirm `plan`/`auto` are valid `--permission-mode` values and
that a positional prompt starts an interactive session, but they do NOT document
whether the positional first turn fires the `UserPromptSubmit` hook. Endless
relies on that hook. The dogfood step treats this as a hard gate: if it does not
fire, stop and report rather than work around it.

## From the description

(1) Stop delivering the initial prompt with tmux send-keys/paste; launch Claude as the tmux window's command with the handoff as its positional prompt argument, via a new endless-go launcher subcommand that is the multiplexer seam (sets @endless_* window options before exec, so no readiness sleep and no SessionStart race).

(2) Because a positional prompt leaves no interactive turn to type the plan slash-command into, drop the forced plan-mode injection and the vestigial --no-plan flag; default spawned sessions to --permission-mode auto (also plumb --permission-mode/--model/--name pass-throughs).

Removes every send-keys call from spawn (including --attach).

Full tmux-driver decoupling remains a separate, not-yet-filed refactor.

fields.description: Rebuild the worktree's endless-go at the start of just land, before the steps that use it, so a rebased worktree never lands with a stale binary that fails integrity checks.
fields.context:
`just land` runs `endless db apply-change` and `endless worktree land`'s record step using the worktree's bin/endless-go, but only runs `just build` AFTER those steps (the trailing 'Refreshing binaries').

No chicken-and-egg — the up-front build needs nothing the land doesn't already have.

fields.analysis:
Method: enumerate real-DB rows whose creation is event-sourced (tasks, decisions, etc.) and confirm each has its originating event (e.g. task.created) in main's committed .endless/db-ledger; report any row whose event is absent from main's committed ledger (only on an unlanded/dropped worktree branch, or missing).

Also characterize the observed duplication: E-1709's task.created is committed BOTH on main (7e207d8d) AND as a redundant worktree-branch commit (3a3aa8b4) — determine whether --db main run from a worktree double-records, and whether that is benign.

Findings-only, not a fix.

fields.title: Stop ledger commit amends orphaning local worktree bases
