fields.context:
canAmend (in internal/events/commit.go) coalesces ledger commits by git-amending main's tip, and refuses when the tip is reachable from origin/* (don't rewrite pushed history) — but that guard checks only REMOTE refs, not LOCAL refs based on the same commit.

After `worktree land` rebases a worktree branch onto main's tip, the next ledger event amends that tip in place, orphaning the SHA the worktree is based on; taskWorktreeDirty (in internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go) then falsely reports the worktree '1 ahead'/dirty and re-landing never clears it (wasted session time on E-1542; no data loss — entries are on main).

The E-1710 audit found E-1209 landed on main (commit 6671bca9, an ancestor of main) yet has no task_landings row, because task.landed event recording (E-1392) postdates it; only 3 sub-1209 tasks ever got backfilled landing rows.

fields.title: Neutralize committed test-fixture ledger events via revert
fields.description: Neutralize the test-fixture events committed to main's ledger, which collide with real task ids on rebuild, by appending reversing entries replay skips, without rewriting history.
fields.notes:
This task is the first consumer of E-1720.

Preventing new pollution is E-1665; rebuild-db robustness to dup/FK is E-1041.
fields.context:
The E-1710 audit found ~36 of 47 committed segment files in main's .endless/db-ledger (~1500 events, ~1/3 of the ledger) are e2e/test-fixture ledgers that create fixture tasks ('smoke epic', 'Coordinate breakdown epic', 'Implement alpha/beta/gamma') reusing real task ids 1..~150.

On a full rebuild-db they collide with real ids (UNIQUE conflicts) and corrupt low-id state.
fields.analysis: Because the ledger is the DB's append-only WAL, the fix is NOT to delete or rewrite the committed segments;

fields.title: Detect current-but-not-projected rows in validate-db

fields.context:
validate-db (ValidateTasks, internal/events/validator.go) replays the committed ledger into a temp DB and compares to the live DB, but only walks projection->live (missing-from-live plus field drift); it deliberately skips live->projection ('Skip this for now').

So a live-DB row with no ledger create -- the WAL-gap class the E-1710 audit found in E-1223/1224 -- is invisible to validate-db.
fields.analysis: scoped to rows created after the ledger-rollout cutoff (~late April 2026) so the known 253-row pre-rollout April baseline doesn't flood the output.

fields.title: Design structured session-handoff output from endless
fields.description: Design having endless own the session-handoff output: the agent calls a command that returns a structured payload, so what the user reads is controlled by endless, not agent prose.
fields.context: At session end the agent produces verbose free-form reports, most of which Mike ignores and must spend energy filtering.

fields.analysis:
# E-1719 execution status & adjudication

## Phase 1 — DONE, landed + assumed. Phase 2 — 177 applied; +10 pending re-run.

The record-only slice (nullable branch, historical `--ts`, explicit-value
`task.landed`) shipped and the 177 confident landings were applied on main.

## CORRECTION: `validate-db` is NOT clean — but it was already dirty pre-E-1719.
My earlier "validate-db clean" claim was wrong; I never ran it against the real
(polluted) ledger. The dirtiness has three PRE-EXISTING causes, none introduced
by this backfill:
1. Task status/vocab drift (`needs_plan`→`unplanned`, `verify`→`unverified`,
   `in_progress`→`underway`) — the ~341 task "mismatches". This is the actual
   comparison noise, unrelated to landings.
2. Sandbox test-tasks leaking into the real ledger (`UNIQUE ... tasks.id` for
   E-1..E-96, foreign node ids) — every `e-NNNN-verify.sh` doing `task add
   --db sandbox` has polluted the real ledger.
3. `task_landings` can't be projected: the projector SKIPS session events
   (projector.go) so its temp `sessions` table is empty — every landing
   with a session_id fails the session FK (E-1443, E-1719 itself, hundreds,
   all predating this work). Separately, ~38 of the backfilled tasks predate
   the event ledger (no `task.created` event, e.g. E-448) so their landings
   fail the task_id FK. Both are pre-existing projector limits; the backfill
   just points 38 more landings at limit #2.

Why the live data is safe regardless: validate-db's pass/fail is the TASK
comparison (the `task_landings` lines are projection warnings, not failures);
the live rows are correct (session NULL, branch NULL, historical dates); and
`rebuild-db` only rebuilds tasks/decisions/decision_relations — it NEVER
rebuilds task_landings, so there is no path that drops the backfilled rows.

Follow-ups worth filing (separate from E-1719): projector should replay session
events + materialize pre-ledger tasks (or validate-db should special-case
task_landings); and the sandbox-events-in-real-ledger pollution.

fields.title: Make landings survive a rebuild
fields.description: Make rebuild-db preserve task landing records, both by letting the projector insert them despite missing sessions and pre-ledger tasks and by copying them back to the real database.
fields.context:
BUILD side: the projector fails to insert nearly every task_landings row — (1) it skips session events (projector.go), so the temp sessions table is empty and every landing carrying a session_id fails the session_id FK; (2) tasks predating the ledger have no task.created event, so their landings fail the task_id FK.

COPY-BACK side, folded in from E-2065: rebuild-db writes back only tasks, decisions and decision_relations, so even a correctly built task_landings never reaches the real DB — and DELETE FROM tasks cascades the live rows away first.

task_deps has the same copy-back gap without the cascade.

Surfaced by E-1719's historical backfill but affects ALL landings.
fields.analysis:
Folded in E-2065 (2026-08-25), which was filed for the copy-back end of this
same gap before E-1935 and this task were found. Measured evidence from that
work follows.

## Correction to this task's original description

It previously read "rebuild-db never rebuilds task_landings (no data loss)".
The first half is true, the parenthetical is not. `DELETE FROM tasks` CASCADES
to task_landings and the copy-back never puts them back, so a completed rebuild
loses landing history outright. Nobody has hit it only because the command
currently aborts before reaching that point.

## Why the abort exists, and why it must not simply be removed

`DELETE FROM tasks` also tries to null `sessions.task_id`; ED-1560's write-once
trigger aborts that; the abort fails the statement and rolls the transaction
back, so nothing is deleted. That is the only thing standing between the command
and the losses below. E-2062 has since replaced the accidental fuse with a
deliberate refusal.

Full transitive FK closure of that DELETE, second hop included:

    task_landings          CASCADE   destroyed, never restored
    session_gates          CASCADE   destroyed, never restored (via epic_id)
      report_judgments     CASCADE   destroyed  (SECOND HOP)
      report_labels        CASCADE   destroyed  (SECOND HOP)
    sessions.task_id       SET NULL  violates ED-1560
    sessions.epic_id       SET NULL
    session_statuses       SET NULL  (dead feature, removed separately)
    decisions.origin_task_id, tasks.parent_id   SET NULL, both restored

task_deps is a quieter variant: the projector builds it, the copy-back skips it,
and no FK reaches it — so a rebuild silently leaves every blocking relation at
whatever the live database happened to hold.

## Traps for the fix

- `tasks_notify_sessions` is AFTER UPDATE ON tasks. Today's delete-then-insert
  never fires it; switching the copy-back to an upsert WOULD, notifying every
  live session about every task whose projected value differs. Suppress the
  notice triggers around any copy-back; e-1969's change file shows the
  drop-then-recreate shape inside a transaction.
- `task_landings_notify_sessions` is AFTER INSERT, so copying landings back
  announces every historical landing to every live session. The E-2005 schema
  comment calls that replay "harmless" ON THE GROUNDS that rebuild copies back
  only three tables — true today, false the moment this lands. Correct it in the
  same commit.
- A projected task_landings.session_id can name a session this machine never
  had: the ledger is shareable, sessions are machine-local. NULL it on copy
  rather than failing the FK.
- `PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF` is not the escape. SQLite ignores it inside a
  transaction, so it would fence the whole replacement and leave dangling rows
  on a genuinely-lost task id. MaxOpenConns is 1, so the usual pooled-connection
  objection does not apply; the reason is correctness.

## Sequencing

This must land before `sessions.task_id` loses its ON DELETE SET NULL, and
E-2062's guard should be deleted only once this is done. Both constraints are
spelled out in E-2062's plan. Cause (1) of the build side — the projector
skipping session events — is shared with E-1041, which absorbed E-1035 for the
same reason; settle who owns `ensureSession` before building.

## From the description

Which tables belong in the copy-back is for the implementor to settle with the user.

fields.title: Isolate sandbox ledger writes from the real project ledger
fields.description: Isolate ledger writes in sandbox mode so events stay in the sandbox instead of being committed to the real project's ledger, where sandbox test tasks pollute production.
fields.notes: Do this BEFORE the cleanup task, else the leak keeps re-accruing.
fields.context:
emit_event resolves project_root from the projects table (the real checkout) and appends+commits event JSONL to the real .endless/db-ledger/ regardless of --db sandbox.

So every sandbox operation — e.g. every 'endless task add --db sandbox' in a tests/tasks/*-verify.sh — permanently writes test-task events (ids 1,2,3... under per-sandbox node ids) into the PRODUCTION ledger, colliding with real E-1..E-96 and making validate-db/rebuild-db noisy.

Surfaced by E-1719's validate-db check.
fields.analysis:
Post-brainstorm constraints for the re-plan (E-1733, 2026-07-05): (1) Architecture governing this task is ED-1525 (ledger follows the active DB context) and ED-1528 (the resolved endless.db config dir is the sole sandbox switch; never key on sandbox-dir existence). (2) --db flag validity is tightened separately by the related self_dev-only bug fix; this task's resolver simply inherits whatever DB context resolution produces. (3) There are FOUR CommitLedgerSegment callsites (the epic-derivation emitter is the fourth), not the three this task's drafted text says. (4) Acceptance script already exists on main: tests/tasks/e-1729-verify.sh — sections B and C are red until this task is done; ALL PASSED is the completion bar. The plan must direct the implementer to maintain/extend that script (adjust invocations if the CLI shape changes, keep it fully isolated from the real DB/ledger) and the verify handoff to Mike must be exactly 'esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1729-verify.sh' — nothing more unless manual verification is truly unavoidable, in which case elaborate. (5) Fix the stale comment at internal/events/commit.go ensureMainCheckout claiming sandbox ledger routing exists. Rationale/alternatives: ED-1525/ED-1528 and E-1733's outcome.

## From the description

Fix: in sandbox mode route the ledger to a sandbox-local db-ledger dir (mirror the DB isolation), or make sandbox emits DB-only.

## Why this is blocked by E-894 (Mike, 2026-08-27)

Not for the reason the pairing suggests. The excision itself does not need the
Go port: it edits `.endless/db-ledger/*.jsonl` by hand, and the read side
(`events.ReadAllEvents` → `ProjectToTempDB`) is already Go.

What blocks it is the second half of this task's own description — "remove
them, then re-derive + validate". `endless-go event rebuild-db --confirm` is
refused on purpose (E-2062), so re-derive can only be a dry-run comparison
today. Repairing it is E-799, which Mike has sequenced behind the port of DB
access to Go because it needs his own focused attention. So this task waits on
the port by way of the rebuild, not by way of the ledger.

Scope, measured 2026-08-27 (full evidence in E-1732's outcome): 1,071 foreign
lines in the real ledger, unchanged since 2026-07-02, so nothing is still
accruing. Under ED-1527's per-line rule the split is 1,047 clearly bug-written
(11 of them occupying real ids 1034-1039), 18 clearly legitimate — node 9000's
16 lines are real 2026-04-27 rollout history, and node 86eb carries two real
E-1542 landings among its fixtures — and 6 needing a call (node abcd's five
E-1628 landings, node b745's one session status). Node-id excision is unsafe:
node 3b27 is a confirmed collision between a 2026-06 writer and sandbox e-1853,
created 2026-08-06.

fields.title: Reject --db in non-self_dev projects
fields.description: Reject --db loudly in projects that are not developing Endless itself, since such a project has exactly one database, instead of silently creating a stray empty one.
fields.context: Today config.apply_db_choice checks only the worktree path shape (no self_dev check), every downstream project's worktrees match it, and db.get_connection then silently mkdirs the sandbox path and creates a fresh empty endless.db in the cache.
fields.analysis:
Decided validation matrix (Mike, 2026-07-05): project not self_dev -> any --db value is an error, main included (a silent no-op masks confusion about what the flag does). Self_dev project -> --db main valid anywhere in the project (worktrees need it to escape the sandbox; the E-1429 gate requires --db there), --db sandbox additionally requires cwd inside a .endless/worktrees/e-NNN worktree (existing check, keep it). Why the hole exists: the self_dev gates were added piecemeal to other layers — gated_worktree_root (the E-1429 requirement gate), the E-1513 re-exec, and Go's SelfDetectWorktreeSandbox — but the validator config.apply_db_choice never got one; it only asks 'is cwd worktree-shaped'. db.get_connection's ensure_config_dir then creates the missing dir + empty DB on first connect, which is what turns the missing check into silent stray state. The rejection message must be plain (no internal task IDs) and say the flag only applies to projects with self_dev enabled. Scope note: sandboxes as a product concept stay open to ALL projects (project-specific files via hook scripts, separate feature); this bug is strictly about the endless.db location flag.

fields.context: .endless/sessions/ is obsolete: nothing writes it, files are 2+ months stale, and the only reference is a stale docstring on session_show_resolve (data now comes from the DB sessions table + tmux).

Leave hidden hard-error stubs at the old top-level names: invoking one exits non-zero with a message naming the new command; not a working alias and not shown in --help.

fields.title: Add a handoff-status command reporting only git anomalies
fields.description: Add a command that inspects the repo for handoff git anomalies, such as uncommitted files, stray tags, unlanded commits or leaked worktrees, and prints nothing when clean.
fields.context:
On session handoff the agent narrates git side-effects (uncommitted files, stray tags, unlanded commits, leaked worktrees, working-tree cleanliness).

Because the spawn prompt enumerates these as categories to report, a clean repo yields 'nothing to report' dressed as reporting — pure noise.

The agent's final message then reduces to what it genuinely can't compute: how-to-verify and the return line.
fields.analysis: This moves the 'is clean worth saying?' judgment out of the agent (which errs toward self-covering) into a tool where empty output IS the representation of clean — the durable fix for this class of noise.

fields.title: Rewrite the spawn-prompt final-message template
fields.description: Rewrite the spawn-prompt closing instructions to a single rule: state a delta only if it is anomalous, otherwise emit only the verification steps and the return line.
fields.context:
The spawn-prompt template's closing instructions enumerate report categories (git side-effects, landed-vs-worktree delta, external state).

Naming an empty category invites the agent to fill it with 'none'.

Cheap, immediate mitigation while the handoff-status command (the durable fix) is built.
fields.analysis: Removing the buckets removes the prompt to confirm-the-negative.

fields.title: Let projects configure allowed paths for the path gate
fields.description: Let a project declare allowed absolute-path patterns in its config that the inline-content path gate accepts alongside its built-in allowed paths.
fields.context:
The path gate (E-1744) blocks absolute paths; its built-in allowed set covers endless's own config+cache dirs.

Other projects using endless as a product have their own well-known outside-root paths that legitimately appear in their plans.
fields.analysis:
merged with the built-in table and per-invocation --allow-path flags at one composition point.

Term: allowed paths, not whitelist.

fields.title: Reopen a done task to revisit when its plan text is edited
fields.description: Reopen a done task to revisit automatically, and announce it, when task update actually changes its plan text, with an option to keep the status.
fields.context:
Editing tasks.text on a task in a done state (assumed/confirmed/completed) adds unshipped scope, making the done-status a lie and leaving the task hidden from session monitor.

Today the agent must remember to set revisit by hand — the wrong layer in a product used across many projects.
fields.analysis:
scoped to text edits (not outcome/analysis), with a --keep-status escape hatch.

Replaces relying on agent memory.

fields.title: Add a gate and doc lint refusing the current user's name

fields.description: Record linking, blocking, unblocking and unlinking a task as a revisited touch in the session's task list, like other task events.

session_tasks captures 'somehow interacted with' a task, not just 'worked on' it (Mike, 2026-07-10).

Today only ten content and lifecycle task events record a touch via upsertSessionTask (internal/events/executor.go): created and imported as surfaced, claimed as goal, and status_changed, fields_updated, moved, deleted, bulk_cleared, landed, released as revisited.

The relation edits (task link, block, unblock, unlink) emit task_dep.created and task_dep.deleted (internal/events/event.go), which have no executor in that touch path, so linking or blocking a task never enrolls it in session_tasks.

fields.title: Hide the active task's uncommitted work from session status

Uncommitted work on the task you're actively working is expected, not an anomaly.

fields.title: Add --ascii flag to session status for copy-safe output
fields.description: Add an --ascii flag to session status that replaces every decorative multibyte glyph with a single-byte ASCII equivalent, so copied output stays intact.
fields.context:
`endless session status` (the endless-go session-status renderer) is a display view that leads each row with a ✎ pencil glyph (U+270E) and truncates titles with a … ellipsis (U+2026), plus tree/box-drawing glyphs.

Those multibyte UTF-8 chars garble when the output is copied as plain text through editors (observed: pasting via pbcopy→nano made task IDs look wrong and they got hand-corrupted).
fields.analysis:
Default output is unchanged; --ascii is opt-in.

Task IDs are already plain ASCII, so only the decoration needs transliterating.

fields.title: Remove tmux return line and spawner task from handoffs

Both predate session monitor/goto and are now noise: session monitor shows the spawning task and session goto returns to it.

Pure removal (no session goto pointer — navigation is a user concern handled by the tmux status line and CLI).

delete the now-dead return_anchor and spawner_task plumbing in task_cmd.py, update the four handoff Python tests, and strike the return-line/spawning-task mentions from the orchestration guide (docs/guide/orchestration.md).

fields.title: Add a task report command for just-the-facts handoffs
fields.description: Add a task report command that computes the handoff facts, checks free-text notes and questions, and steers the agent to relay only those facts, plainly.
fields.notes:
Persisting reports as queryable rows is E-1777.

Full spec in --text; rationale in E-1760 outcome and ED-1531/ED-1532.
fields.analysis:
Input is a small JSON payload (notes/questions only); stdout is a steering prompt (not a verbatim relay); no intermediate XML.

Check wording lives in a user-editable config surface; the Haiku model is fixed.

fields.title: Emit a task report reminder on terminal status-set
fields.description: Emit a reminder from the status-update command when an agent winds a task down, routing this handoff and further session reporting through the task report command.
fields.notes: Full rationale in E-1760 outcome.
fields.analysis:
Nudge in the reminder, gate in the command; no hook (a CLI command can do it).

Fires ONLY on the agent-driven wind-down transitions: underway->unverified, ->assumed, and ->completed with --outcome.

Does NOT fire on submitted, ready, confirmed, claim/underway, or the revisit/declined/obsolete management transitions.

fields.title: Add a FULL STATUS bypass keyword and mid-session guidance
fields.description: Add spawn-prompt guidance routing mid-session and end-of-session reporting through the task report command, plus a user keyword that allows one unconstrained response.
fields.notes: Full rationale in E-1760 outcome.
fields.analysis:
The keyword itself lives in the same tunable config surface so it can be renamed.

This is the 'elaborate when I ASK, shut up when I have not' lever.

fields.title: Analyze session handoffs to propose task report XML elements
fields.description: Analyze about 25 recent session handoffs, classify the concerns each raised, and propose from that the elements and attributes for the task report's XML payload.
fields.analysis:
'XML schema' meant informally: what elements and attributes are needed.

Deliverable partitions each concern into computed (from handoff-status), validated-value (with none allowed), or free-text escape hatch, and names which ceremony categories the schema deliberately gives no element to.

Full method in --text.

fields.title: Render markdown tables correctly in endless-go render
fields.description: Render GitHub-flavored markdown tables as aligned columns in the terminal markdown renderer behind task show, instead of raw pipe rows.
fields.notes: E-1746's plan deliberately let code fences and tables overflow rather than being mangled, to avoid glamour-style prose reflow — but the result is that table pipe rows are emitted as raw un-aligned lines rather than rendered as aligned columns.
fields.analysis:
Reference: glow renders tables via glamour → lipgloss/table (github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss table/resizing.go). Its resizer computes per-column min/max/median cell widths, expands-to-fill when narrow, and shrinks via three passes (shave columns >= half-width, shave most-over-median, shave biggest) with NO floor. Two flaws we deliberately avoid: (1) headers are hard-coded to height 1 even with wrap on, so a shrunk column TRUNCATES the header with … ('Frequency'→'Fr…'); we instead wrap headers to 3 rows then truncate WITH a legend. (2) shrink uses cell-width min/median, never the longest word, so a column can be squeezed below its longest token and lipgloss then breaks mid-character ('high'→'hig'/'h'); we instead set a computed minCol floor = floor(W/(N*2.5)) and hard-break only tokens that exceed the allocated width.

Why build our own allocator, not import lipgloss/table: (a) it bakes in both flaws above; (b) it pulls in lipgloss + x/ansi, breaking mdterm's deliberate 'no third-party style deps, same surface as the goldmark parser' design; (c) it over-pads (expands to fill full width). We borrow its ideas (min/max/median, shrink-biggest, shrink-to-median), not its code.

Panning: less 668 pans horizontally on-demand via arrow keys (man: RIGHTARROW '...acts as though -S were in effect' while scrolled), so we need NOT launch with -S (which would break the prose no-reflow-but-soft-wrap design). less slides raw text (half-screen default step), not column-snapping like a TUI grid, so it's gentler than teagrid — but we still cap column width (maxColFraction ~0.65W, hard cap W-minCol) so >=2 columns stay visible and panning reads as sliding.

Constants (minColDivisor 2.5, maxHeaderRows 3, targetMaxRows 6, maxColFraction 0.65) have no closed-form optimum — they are balanced empirically via the eyeball-tuning harness in the plan.

## From the description

Fix the renderer to detect table blocks and render them with aligned columns (padded cells, separator row drawn) while preserving the no-reflow behavior for prose.

Verify via 'endless task show <id> -p' on a task whose text contains a table.

fields.title: Add endless session resume for lost Claude sessions
fields.description: Add 'endless session resume' to relaunch, in the current pane, a Claude session orphaned when tmux crashes, resolving a task id, session id or Claude id prefix to it and its worktree.
fields.analysis:
Resolves <ref> (a task id as shown on the tmux tab, a session id, or a Claude UUID prefix) to the session's UUID and its task worktree, cd's into the worktree, and execs `claude --resume <uuid>` so the resumed session takes over the current pane.

Resolution is task-first and, unlike `session goto`, includes ended sessions, since a crash takes every session to a dead pane.

The task->session lookup runs in Go via a `session-query resume-target` verb (no new Python SQLite reads).

fields.title: Derive test regression from the last-green baseline
fields.description: Derive whether a failing test is a regression or never worked by comparing its run to the last passing baseline in captured test history, rather than asking the agent.
fields.notes:
Split out of E-1771.

Blocked by E-1777: regression can only be derived once test-run history is captured as structured rows.
fields.analysis:
NOT asserted by the agent (a single session lacks a trustworthy baseline; asking it to classify invites 'probably not my fault' self-cover).

Frame the result as a recoverability signal — 'this test has a known-green ancestor, so a working version exists in VCS' — not blame; most meaningful at project scope.

fields.title: Replace less with a pannable terminal viewer
fields.description: Replace the external less pager used by task show with a built-in terminal viewer that pans horizontally and scrolls vertically, so wide tables render at natural width.
fields.context:
E-1775 makes markdown tables always fit the screen width and rely on vertical scroll, because less -R wraps any over-width line into an unreadable mess (it only pans on manual arrow-chop, and launching with -S would also chop the soft-wrapped prose).

That is a stopgap: a genuinely wide table gets squeezed into narrow, tall columns with no way to see the full-width layout.
fields.analysis:
Mike's go-tealeaves teagrid (a BubbleTea grid pager) is prior art and a likely basis; this also drops the external less dependency (the E-1746 deferred note).

Scope to settle when planned: general pager vs table-aware grid, less fallback, pan interaction model.

fields.title: Document session navigation commands in the sessions guide

'Run all tests' is a fiction once a real project has multiple test tiers — unit, integration, e2e, smoke — that differ in cost, runtime, scope, isolation needs, and flakiness.

fields.description: Reduce what the user must review twice by keeping agents from narrating what the tools already compute, as in end-of-session handoffs and plan recaps, leaving only genuine open decisions.

fields.title: Fix path gate blocking relative-path tokens as absolute
fields.description: Fix the inline-content path gate to block only genuine absolute paths, not relative tokens like pytest/uv or a lone slash, and correct its advice message.
fields.context:
Two observed cases: a relative-path-form token like pytest/uv (a runner type/subtype, intended to be allowed), and a bare/standalone slash such as '/' used as an illustrative delimiter in prose.

Surfaced filing and later correcting E-1789's decisions (ED-1535/1536/1537), where both cases had to be worked around with --allow-path.
fields.analysis:
(no prior analysis)

# Fresh evidence for part 2, the message's advice ordering (2026-08-31, ES-1159)

Filing content for E-2094, `task update --description` was refused for a genuine
absolute path — an illustrative macOS temp prefix quoted inside an explanation
OF that prefix. The gate was correct; part 1 of this task does not apply.

Part 2 does, and it cost a turn. The message ends:

    Put real content inline, or author scratch under .endless/tmp/ and load it
    with --description-file; a cross-project file can be referenced by a Git
    URL. To keep this path, add --allow-path with a regex matching it.

I read the whole message and still rephrased the prose to remove the paths,
because rephrasing is the first remedy offered and --allow-path is the last
clause of the last sentence. Mike's reaction: "you flabbergast me by avoiding
--allow-path; I asked for --allow-path precisely so you would not have to
rephrase."

So the ordering does not merely bury the flag — it actively selects against it.
An agent takes the first sanctioned option it is given, and here that option
distorts the content to satisfy the check, which is the opposite of what the
gate is for. Leading with --allow-path, as this task already proposes, would
have produced the right behaviour with no judgement required.

Second observation for the same part: the message recommends --description-file
for a DESCRIPTION. Descriptions are single-line and capped at 1024 characters,
so that advice cannot help — and following it produced a second refusal
("Description must be a single line") on the next attempt.

## From the description

It must block only genuine absolute paths (a leading slash followed by a path), not relative tokens, notation, or a lone slash.

Mike flags this may be a bigger issue needing discussion before implementing.

lead with --allow-path (currently last) and stop recommending --description-file for descriptions (which are short inline metadata); keep the flag, just don't promote it in this message.

fields.title: Surface upstream blocker chains in session status
fields.description: Surface the full upstream chain of prerequisites blocking every task shown in session status, not just the tasks the current task blocks.
fields.context: `endless session status` surfaces the tasks the focal task BLOCKS (one hop downstream) but never the tasks BLOCKING it.
fields.analysis:
# Why this, and the deliberate choices

## Direction asymmetry: blockers walk the chain, children do not
`session status` today (internal/monitor/session_status.go → SessionStatusRows)
walks `dep_type='blocks'` in the DOWNSTREAM direction only — the focal's direct
dependents (one hop, E-1685) plus direct children (E-1691). Both are capped at
one hop to avoid exploding an epic's subtree into the pane.

This task adds the UPSTREAM walk (`blocked_by`) and makes it TRANSITIVE, for
every task already in the view — not just the focal. The asymmetry is
deliberate: children fan out (an epic can have dozens), so a transitive child
walk would flood the pane; blocker chains are narrow (each task has few
prerequisites), so walking the full chain stays bounded in practice.

## Escape valve (deferred — NOT built here)
If a specific blocker chain does get noisy, the intended fix is a command to
HIDE a given task from session status — an edge-case release valve — rather
than pre-capping blocker depth. Deferred until the problem is actually felt;
filing/building it now would be speculative.

## Why it's worth doing: makes coarse / idealistic blocks visible
An upstream block that is too coarse (a task dragged behind a whole epic when it
needs only a sliver) or merely idealistic (ideally-first, not literally
required) currently drags work SILENTLY — the gate is never shown. Surfacing the
upstream chain is what makes such blocks visible so they can be corrected. This
does NOT resolve the over-blocking problem itself (that is E-1708); it exposes
it. Related axis already in the model: hard block = `blocks`, soft/advisory =
`relates_to`; E-876 set the status-based release (verify blocks, assumed
unblocks).

## Concrete motivating case
E-1671 (upcasting-pipeline epic, unplanned) is the head of the chain
E-1671 → E-1659 → E-1658 → E-1536. None of it surfaces in this session even
though E-1536 (a direct dependent of the focal E-1533) IS shown — because the
view never walks upstream. That gap — losing sight of the real front of the
line — is what this task closes.

## From the description

Children stay one-hop (fan-out risk); blockers walk the full chain (narrower).

fields.title: Document follow-up loop and slice-extraction practices
fields.description: Document two practices in the session guide: a session closes its discovery loop by chasing blockers and filing follow-ups, and a small slice of a blocker can be extracted instead of waiting.
fields.analysis:
(1) A session does not stop at its bound task's implementation — it closes the discovery loop: walk session status, chase blockers, file+plan follow-ups. fields.analysis:
# E-1803 — enforcement design for the no-ceremony report channel

## Problem (demonstrated live)
`task report` (E-1771) computes the clean facts and bounces ceremonial `--json`
entries, but the agent still authors the surrounding chat message and can append
"helpful" prose. Observed: the agent ran `task report`, relayed its two lines, then
hand-wrote a redundant regression paragraph with no action item for the user — on
top of output the harness had already captured.

## Why NOT a Stop-hook bounce
A Stop hook that rejects a message diverging from the report forces the agent to
REGENERATE the turn — more tokens, more latency, the exact waste this feature exists
to remove. Enforcing an anti-waste feature with a mechanism that multiplies waste is
self-defeating. A text-diff hook also can't tell an ALLOWED open-decision from
editorializing without the semantic check `report` already owns.

## Structural limit (state it plainly in the impl — do not over-promise a gate)
Claude Code always lets the model author the final natural-language message. No
tool's stdout REPLACES that message, and no hook edits it in place. So "report
authors the whole turn" is not achievable as a hard gate; the honest ceiling is a
strong, well-placed nudge.

## Mechanism this task adds (the enforcement arm)
A `PostToolUse` hook matched to the Bash call that runs `endless task report`
returns `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` (the recently-added field; also
available on `UserPromptSubmit` / `SessionStart`). Delivery: the harness captures
the command's stdout, fires the hook with that output on the hook's stdin, then
folds the hook's `additionalContext` into the model's context INLINE, tied to that
tool result (surfaced like a `<system-reminder>`) — not a parallel stream. Content:
instruct the model to emit the report output verbatim as its entire reply and add
nothing. This lands at compose time, contextual and harness-authoritative — the
strongest in-harness lever short of a regenerate loop, but a strong nudge, NOT a lock.

## Coverage arm (unchanged from the original filing)
Make `task report` the invoked channel at every in-session user-facing checkpoint,
not just session end/status. Acceptable output defined FUNCTIONALLY: a computed
fact the user cannot derive XOR a genuine open decision/blocker, else nothing —
report's `notes` vs `questions`. Derive from function; do not enumerate situations
(an enumerated list drifts the moment a new surface appears).

## Enforcement-arm ceiling and the bypass hole (session 2026-07-29, Mike + agent)

Both arms above anchor to a tool call — the PostToolUse nudge to the `task
report` invocation, the coverage arm to whatever action defines a checkpoint.
That leaves a **bypass hole**: output at a *toolless* turn (a "here's what I
found" reply that calls nothing) is invisible to any tool-anchored hook. It is
also, notably, the case where verbose prose is most often *legitimate*, so it is
the lowest-value and highest-false-positive place to gate.

Rejected fix — a standing per-turn `UserPromptSubmit` injection of the functional
rule: injecting identical context every turn habituates (boy-who-cried-wolf) and
the model stops attending to it. A functional wording does not rescue it; the
repetition, not the wording, is what kills the signal.

Evidence the residual is compliance, not a missing trigger: in the demonstrated
failure the agent had *already* been nudged — `task update --status unverified`
printed "Report through the command… Relay its output verbatim; add nothing" —
and appended two redundant paragraphs anyway. So the structured checkpoints
(status flip, plan save, commit) already carry a trigger; adding more triggers
does not help, because the binding constraint is the structural ceiling (the
harness always lets the model author the final message), not trigger placement.

The `Stop` hook (verified against the Claude Code hooks docs): fires at the end
of **every** main-agent turn (not `/exit`-only), receives `last_assistant_message`
directly, and supports observe-only (exit 0). It is the *only* hook that sees the
turn's output independent of any tool call, so it is the sole place that could
watch the toolless-turn hole. But its levers are all weak against the live turn:
observe-only logs the message a turn too late (the user has already read it);
`decision:block` forces regeneration — the exact waste this feature rejects;
`additionalContext` at `Stop` only primes the *next* turn. So `Stop`'s honest
role is **measurement, not a gate** — feed the scrivener pattern into the report
persistence / regression signals (E-1777 / E-1778) to keep drift visible and
tunable. A `Stop` detector also needs the same semantic classifier `report`
already owns (narration-that-should-have-been-report vs. a genuine substantive
answer); a dumb "long message + no report call" heuristic false-positives on
legitimate discussion turns and just relocates the cry-wolf problem to the
metrics layer.

Net: there is no hard gate to be had — the ceiling is real and no hook lifts it.
The higher-leverage half is **source removal**, not another nudge: fold the
handoff's "state the regression result in one line" instruction into a computed
`report` fact (E-1778), so the handoff stops *asking* the agent to narrate a
clean result. Removing the prompt that licenses the prose has no ceiling;
nudging against it does.

## From the description

(2) ENFORCEMENT: add a PostToolUse hook matched to the task report Bash invocation that injects hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext telling the agent to relay the report output verbatim and add nothing — a contextual, compose-time, harness-authoritative nudge.

Honest limit (see analysis): Claude Code can't make the tool output BE the agent's message, so this is the strongest in-harness lever short of a regenerate loop — a strong nudge, not a hard gate.

fields.analysis:
# What `tasks.tier` is today

Surveyed by ES-1102, revised in E-1815 after the questions this was gathered to
answer were settled in conversation. File references name symbols rather than
line numbers, which go stale on every land.

## Shape

- `tasks.tier` is a bare nullable `INTEGER` on `tasks` (`internal/schema/schema.sql`).
  No FK, no values table — it predates the enum-as-integer-FK convention the
  ratings work (ED-1538) follows.
- Its labels exist only in Python: `0=n/a, 1=auto, 2=quick, 3=deep, 4=discuss`
  (`_TIER_LABELS`, `src/endless/task_cmd.py`). The Go side reads the raw int.

## Actual use in the real ledger

| tier | rows |
|---|---|
| NULL | 187 |
| 0 (n/a) | 1052 |
| 1 (auto) | 12 — all `ready` |
| 2 (quick) | 4 |
| 3 (deep) | 4 |
| 4 (discuss) | 8 |

28 meaningfully-rated rows out of ~1250. The field is, in practice, unused.

## Why it is invisible

`task show` renders the Tier line under `if item["tier"]:` (`task_cmd.py`) —
falsy for **both** NULL and 0. With 1239 of 1267 rows at NULL-or-0, the line is
absent for ~98% of tasks. That is the reported "does not even show up in
`task show`": not a missing renderer, a guard the data almost never clears.
E-1233 already owns adding the line properly.

## What tier still drives

- `--tier 1` auto-advances a pre-work task (`untriaged`/`unplanned`) to `ready`
  and exempts it from triage (`task_cmd.py`).
- `task next --tier` filter; the `task list` Tier column and its sort key.
- The tmux status line and the session-notice headline
  (`internal/monitor/session_notices.go`, `internal/monitor/tmux_lookup.go`).
- The task change-tracking trigger (`internal/schema/schema.sql`).
- Documented in `docs/guide/tasks.md` (the `--tier` flag rows and the
  `--keep-status` auto-transition table).

## Resolution (E-1815)

**Complexity replaces tier.** Tier's ladder — auto → quick → deep → discuss — is
a human-interaction-depth scale, and ED-1539 defines complexity as "how much
human-AI interaction is needed to nail down the specifics." Same judgment, two
names. Tier's only behavior, the `--tier 1` auto-`ready`, is something complexity
could carry identically, so tier has no behavior complexity cannot absorb and no
meaning it does not duplicate.

**Do not reverse-engineer tier's intent.** It predates current thinking, is ~2%
populated, and is entangled with the shelved background-tasks work. Design
complexity and risk from ED-1538 and ED-1539 directly. Tier is a column to
remove, not a design to reconcile with.

**Do not carry `--tier 1`'s auto-`ready` forward.** A rating value does not move
status; status routing is triage plus approve, consistent with E-1844 ("with
status — not complexity/risk — routing the workflow"). E-1153, which was specced
as shorthand for `--tier 1 --phase now --status ready`, is obsoleted, so nothing
depends on the shortcut.

**Do not spend effort on the "gate collision."** An earlier revision of this
analysis framed `--tier 1` reaching `ready` without approval as a hole in
ED-1538's approval gate. Judged in E-1815 as overstated: work happens in
worktrees and there is no auto-land, so an agent reaching `ready` on its own has
no path to harm short of going haywire, at which point there are larger problems.
Recorded so the thread is not reopened.

**Migration cost is low.** The 1052 tier-0 rows mean "n/a" — nothing to migrate.
28 rows carry meaning. The remainder is mechanical code surface: CLI
parse/filter/display, the Go monitor readers, the schema change-trigger, and the
guide docs.

## One open question worth carrying

Tier reached 28 meaningfully-rated rows out of ~1250. Whatever suppressed its
adoption may suppress complexity's too. Two candidates, both addressed by the
design below but worth confirming rather than assuming: nothing ever *required* a
tier (agent-proposes-at-submit does require a rating), and the value was
invisible in `task show` for ~98% of tasks (E-1233 fixes the render guard).

## Not this

`src/endless/models.py` carries an unrelated `tier: int = 5` on the
project-discovery model. Same word, different concept — do not conflate.

## From the description

nullable FK columns to seeded complexity_levels and risk_levels tables (low=1, medium=3, high=5; 2 and 4 unseeded), Go int-const enums with String()/Parse(), agent-proposed at submit and user-ratified at approve.

Ratings do not move status.

Tier is removed rather than kept — it is the same judgment under another name, ~2% populated, and carries no behavior complexity cannot absorb.

fields.analysis:
# Design captured (delivery arm PENDING E-1803)

Two separable axes. Axis 1 (content and templates) is independent and plannable
now. Axis 2 (delivery) rides on E-1803's PostToolUse mechanism and must NOT be
finalized until E-1803 is implemented and proven.

## Decision: uniform relocation

A claimed-in session ALWAYS relocates its working directory into the task's new
worktree -- no type-dependent exception. Rationale: staying in the main checkout
risks running tools against the main branch instead of the worktree branch (the
worse failure). No-code tasks are not no-touch: brainstorm and research record
their outcome to the git-tracked db-ledger, which must be merged -- so they too
produce a landable artifact and belong in the worktree. The wrapper's job is to
make the relocation and the resulting --db main routing impossible to forget
(that routing switch is exactly the thing that must not be dropped).

## Axis 1 -- content (plannable now)

Split each type's handoff into (a) invariant type-mechanics and (b) arrival
framing. Shape: a shared partial plus per-context wrappers (the spawn wrapper is
the existing framing; the claim wrapper is new). Discipline: each partial earns
its existence from a genuinely invariant shared concern; reach for a conditional
only when the alternative is three-plus near-identical partials; lift to shared
DATA only where a drift between renderings would be a bug (terminal status, the
one-session-one-task rule); do not pre-factor -- let the second real consumer
pull each seam.

## Claim wrapper content (arrival block, claim-only)

Focused, not thin. Beyond the shared type-mechanics partial it must carry:
- you are NOT freshly spawned; you have been running and just claimed this -- no
  blank-slate assumption;
- relocate: move your working directory into the task's new worktree (a spawned
  session is born there; a claimed-in one is not);
- routing: the worktree routes DB access to the sandbox, so real-ledger updates
  need --db main;
- fold the planning you already did into the task (the task update text field),
  not left in chat.

## Axis 2 -- delivery (PENDING E-1803)

Candidate: a PostToolUse hook matched to the endless task claim invocation
returns hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext carrying the claim wrapper, folded
inline against that tool result (the same lever E-1803 prototypes for task
report). NOT settled -- E-1803 is unbuilt and its own analysis rates the
mechanism a strong nudge, not a hard gate. Finalize only after E-1803 lands and
the mechanism is proven; if E-1803 finds it weak or unworkable, redesign
delivery here.

## From the description

Fix direction: on claim into a live session, inject the type-handoff mechanics into that session's context.

fields.title: Require surfaced facts to be verified against live state
fields.description: Require any fact an agent surfaces to be verified against live state, such as git, the ledger or the file, at that moment, never inferred or recalled from earlier context.
fields.notes: Distinct from E-1803, which governs output VOLUME; this governs output VERACITY.
fields.context: E-1803's report-channel gate ('surface a computed fact the user can't derive XOR a genuine open decision, else nothing') assumes the surfaced fact is TRUE. The costliest agent outputs are confidently-wrong facts the user must track down to disprove -- worse than ceremony.
fields.analysis:
Live evidence (this session): 'relates E-1085' was asserted and linked without checking E-1085's topic (it was about co-developed dependencies, unrelated) -- the user had to catch it. 'The worktree is empty overhead' was asserted without checking git, which held the landable synthesis commit. Both are the expensive failure mode: a false 'helpful' fact the user must chase down to disprove. The lightweight catch for the citation class: when agent-authored text names a task or decision id, resolve it and flag non-existent or topically-mismatched targets before the message lands.

## From the description

a wrong fact must clear a HIGHER bar than an omitted one.

Some classes are mechanically catchable and worth a lightweight check: an agent-authored task-ID citation whose target doesn't resolve or is topically unrelated, or a state claim git contradicts.

fields.description: Author and publish a standalone VISION.md describing what Endless is meant to become, separate from the README and roadmap, drawing on its key tenets and its single-to-multi-developer arc.
fields.analysis:
## Source material for VISION.md

**The arc.** Endless began as a way for one developer to manage many concurrent
Claude Code sessions — first across terminal tabs, then across tmux windows. The
envisioned future is a substrate for many developers collaborating on the same
projects, each driving many AI-agent sessions.

**Core tenets to develop as narrative:**

1. **Humans managing ~2 orders of magnitude more concurrent work.** The human's
   job shifts from doing the work to steering many Claude Code sessions —
   research, coding, bug-fixing, and brainstorming.
2. **A task-centric loop.** The human has Claude Code file task(s), collaborates
   with it on a plan, then spawns each task into its own Claude Code session in a
   new tmux window with a task-specific git worktree and a config/DB sandbox. The
   session works the plan and hands back a verification script that gives the
   human confidence to land — merging the worktree back to `main`.
3. **Collaboration via git, not a server.** Several developers share one project
   by ordinary push/pull; each rebuilds their local view from the same committed
   history; no central authority; contributors never collide.
4. **The DB ledger as the foundation.** A JSONL write-ahead log is the source of
   record, with a rebuildable local DB and per-task isolation — behind-the-scenes
   plumbing that makes the collaboration above viable.

**Give headline billing to:** lowering the human's review burden. Agents report
in structured, skimmable form and don't make the human re-review what the tool
already computed. This is a core Endless philosophy and deserves a prominent place
in the narrative.

## From the description

Distinct from ROADMAP.md and README; deliberately not under the ROADMAP epic.

Sources: Mike's Key Tenets, the single-dev->multi-dev arc, and the lower-review-burden philosophy given headline billing.

fields.title: Fix the title verb gate treating classifier failures as no
fields.description: Fix the title verb gate to tell transient classifier failures apart from a definitive not-a-verb answer, retrying the transient ones and offering a reword only on a real no.
fields.analysis:
Corrected framing (supersedes the earlier analysis on this task): verb validation exists to stop the AI agent from freelancing title vocabulary that is hard for the human to reason about. The bug is NOT that a legitimate verb can be lost — losing a verb is a non-problem. The bug is that _check_verb_via_haiku (src/endless/task_cmd.py) collapses every non-YES outcome into one (False, None), so a CLASSIFIER ERROR (timeout, non-zero exit incl. auth, missing binary, empty/malformed/hedged reply) is handled identically to a definitive NO: the agent is offered a reword and quietly freelances a different title — bypassing validation on an error the human never sees. Repro: "streamline" was rejected on a transient classifier failure and silently reworded to "Explore streamlining...".

## Behavior — three buckets
- Clean YES: register the verb, pass. (unchanged)
- Clean NO (explicitly matched): reject; the title must start with an actual verb, so the agent rewrites it. (unchanged — this is validation working, and is already handled today.)
- Any error / cannot-determine (everything that is not a clean YES or a clean NO): STOP. Do not reword, do not auto-register, do not guess. Surface the actual error to the human and ask how to proceed. Retrying a few times on a transient failure before declaring cannot-determine is fine; the terminal state is a human decision, never an agent reword.

Error subtype does NOT branch behavior — every error leads to the same action (stop + ask). But the stop-and-ask message SHOULD name the specific failure so the human knows what happened: timeout, malformed/nonsensical reply, missing `claude` binary, or non-zero exit (incl. auth). The granularity is for the report, not for control flow.

## Enforcement (the crux — to be designed in the plan)
A "stop and ask" message is insufficient: the agent can (and did) ignore it and reword anyway. The stop must be an ENFORCED GATE the agent cannot bypass — via the Claude hook — so a classifier error halts the agent and hands the decision to the human instead of letting it silently pick different vocabulary. Likely shape: the CLI refuses on a classifier error AND a hook blocks further task-mutation until the human resolves. Working out that gate mechanism is the substance of the plan.

## Rejected
Fork A (auto-register the verb provisionally on a classifier error) is rejected: auto-admitting unreviewed verbs is exactly the agent-freelancing that validation exists to prevent. "Preserving the verb" is not a goal.

Distinct from E-1837 (punctuation/dedup on the verb WRITE path); this is failure-handling on the CLASSIFY path.

## From the description

Replace the boolean check with a named-outcome result that distinguishes the failure modes, retries the transient ones, and offers reword only on a definitive NO. See analysis for the full outcome taxonomy and retry policy.

fields.title: Inject a run-endless-guide pointer at first session start
fields.description: Inject a one-time 'Run endless guide to learn the workflow' line into the first session-start context, so agents in any project using Endless learn the workflow.
fields.context: Surfaced while rewriting README (E-1832).
fields.analysis:
Endless tells THIS repo's agent to run `endless guide` only because the dogfooding repo's committed CLAUDE.md says "First: run endless guide". A downstream project that uses Endless as a product gets no such pointer: the Claude SessionStart / UserPromptSubmit hook (internal/hookcmd/claude.go, buildTaskContextInjection) injects the active task list and inter-session message banners but never mentions the guide, and setup.py never writes anything into a downstream CLAUDE.md. So product users' agents have no reliable way to learn the Endless workflow.

Ship the pointer in the product, not in per-machine config: add a one-shot "Run `endless guide` to learn the Endless workflow" line to the first-time SessionStart context injection (alongside the task-list injection, gated by the same HasInjectedContext one-shot marker so it is not repeated every prompt). This keeps README.md human-only (the guide is agent-formatted and is not routed to humans there) while making the guide reachable by every agent on every project that has the hook installed, regardless of that project's CLAUDE.md.

Surfaced while rewriting README.md (E-1832): the README dropped its human-facing `endless guide` block on the assumption that CLAUDE.md covers the agent path — true only for the dogfooding repo.

Pinned wording (inject verbatim, as the lead line of the first-injection context, before the task list):
New to this project? Run `endless guide` to learn the Endless workflow.

## From the description

Add a one-shot "Run endless guide to learn the workflow" line to the first-time SessionStart context injection so every agent learns the workflow regardless of its project CLAUDE.md.

fields.analysis:
# Evidence: why automatic triage never fires where tasks are filed

Gathered 2026-08-13 during the E-1958 brainstorm. The prescription lives in this
task's plan text; this is only the trace behind it.

## The suppression's premise does not hold on this path

`triage.inline_suppressed()` returns a suppression reason for "self-dev worktree
pinned to the real ledger", mirroring `internal/jobs`'s `suppressedWithReason`.
The mirrored rationale is that candidate code must not write the real ledger.

Traced under `--db main` from inside a worktree:

- `triage.spawn_detached` launches `sys.argv[0]` — the `endless` shim. `just
  install` runs `uv tool install -e .` from the MAIN checkout, so the shim
  resolves to main's source. CLAUDE.md forbids installing editable from a
  worktree.
- The child writes via `event_bridge._resolve_endless_go()`, whose documented
  behavior is: prefer `<worktree>/bin/endless-go` under `--db sandbox`,
  otherwise fall back to the PATH-resolved global.

So under `--db main` both the Python and the Go halves are landed code. The DB
router had already closed the door the suppression guards.

Corroborating: the justfile's `verify` recipe invokes `endless --db sandbox task
verify`, i.e. the global shim; only the `test` recipe's `uv run pytest` resolves
worktree Python. Nothing in normal use runs candidate Python via the `endless`
command.

Where the same rule IS correct: the Claude hooks written into a worktree's
`.claude/settings.json` invoke `<worktree>/bin/endless-go`, which is genuinely
candidate. `internal/jobs`'s suppression protects that; triage copied it without
re-deriving it.

## What is and is not already race-safe

Safe — sweep vs. sweep across processes. `internal/jobs` claims with a CAS lease
(one conditional UPDATE whose WHERE clause is the precondition) and takes every
due/expiry comparison from SQLite's clock, so N processes share one clock. The N
`session monitor` instances that each call `jobs.RunDue` contend and one wins.
`triagejob`'s Schedule sets `LeaseTTL` explicitly from `batchLimit *
perTaskTimeout + leaseHeadroom`, not from Interval, so shortening the interval
does not shrink the lease.

NOT safe — inline vs. sweep. `spawn_detached` invokes `endless triage run --task
N` directly, bypassing the jobs runner entirely, so it holds no lease. A sweep
firing during an inline child's model call re-selects the same still-`untriaged`
row and pays for a second model call. Python's post-call re-read guards the
write but not the spend.

Latent today only because the suppression means the inline path never runs in a
worktree. Fixing the suppression makes it live.

## Errors are unobservable

`spawn_detached` routes all three stdio streams to DEVNULL, on top of a
`triage.run` that is fail-open by design — timeout, missing `claude`, non-zero
exit and unparseable verdict all leave the task `untriaged` without a sound. A
crashed child and a considered no-verdict are indistinguishable, and neither is
recorded anywhere.

## Scale of the symptom

137 live worktrees under `.endless/worktrees/`. Agents file the large majority of
tasks, from worktrees, with `--db main`. So the suppressed path is the normal
path, and the 15-minute sweep is the effective triage latency for nearly every
task filed.

## From the description

For each untriaged task it assembles the persisted-artifact context (description + parent + sibling titles + linked decisions — deliberately NOT the filing session's context) and calls a model via the shared run_internal_claude helper with a config-resolved model (standardize the config key so verb auto-registration and this job resolve their model the same way; do not hardcode 'claude -p'; see E-1849 for making the harness itself pluggable). It then sets status to submitted or unplanned and emits the transition as an event with triager attribution. Runs as belt (inline at file time) and suspenders (background sweep over the untriaged queue).

fields.title: Explore how decisions are carried on tasks
fields.description: Explore the storage shape and lifecycle for decisions carried on tasks, a more organic way to arrive at them, and the relation verb linking a task to a decision that binds it.
fields.notes: Now that the direction is settled to move decisions back onto tasks (E-1868),
fields.analysis:
## The relation verb for a task bound by a decision

Raised 2026-09-11 while planning E-2128, and folded in here rather than filed
separately: E-1868 removes the task/decision split, so anything built against
`decision_relations` today is work the move deletes.

**`implements` is wrong, and is banned in prose.** An architectural decision is
a standing constraint, not a specification that some task realises and retires.
ED-1589 ("a display never computes an expensive answer to paint a row") binds
every display surface built from now on, so "E-2128 implements ED-1589" claims a
completion that cannot happen — and if it could, the next display surface would
be free to compute. Mike's analogy: a homeowner deciding on midcentury modern
does not then write house plans titled "Implement my midcentury modern home".

`implements` is defensible only for a ONE-TIME commitment — "migrate to
Postgres" — where the decision really is carried out once and then stands. Most
decisions worth recording are rules, not migrations. The relation type is
currently named `implemented_by`, carrying the same flaw at the schema level;
this is the moment to fix it, since the storage is being rebuilt anyway.

**Candidates Mike raised:** complies with, conforms to, respects, follows,
obeys, defers to, honors, adheres to, aligns with, per.

Notes toward choosing, not a choice:

- `per` is the dominant form in the existing corpus by a wide margin, but it is
  a preposition, so it works as an inline citation and not as a relation name.
- `follows` reads best in prose, but its inverse "followed by" collides with
  temporal ordering, which a task tracker cannot afford to blur.
- `defers to` implies yielding in a conflict rather than being built within a
  constraint, which is a different relation.
- `obeys` and `honors` are anthropomorphic; `aligns with` is weaker than the
  relation actually is.
- `conforms to` has no temporal ambiguity and its natural inverse is a real verb
  (`constrains` / `governs`) rather than an awkward passive — matching the
  asymmetric pair `documents`/`implements` the schema already uses.

**Pick the inverse at the same time.** The decision side needs a natural reading.
"Implemented by" was tolerable; "conformed to by" is not.

**Whatever is chosen must let a task SHOW the decisions that bind it.**
`endless task show` renders task-to-task relations only — ED-1589 links to
E-2128 and appears nowhere in `task show E-2128` — so a session reading its own
task cannot see which decisions constrain it. That gap is why tasks acquired the
habit of announcing the decision in their opening line. E-2131 was filed against
the current schema to fix the rendering and was declined as work E-1868 deletes;
the requirement belongs here instead.



## The merge: what the discussion of 2026-09-13 settled

Worked through with Mike. Recorded here rather than as decisions, because these
are design calls for this epic's tree, not standing constraints on the project.

### Decisions get TWO homes, not one

- `tasks.type='decision'` identifies an ARCHITECTURAL decision. Type is the
  right carrier because it is already the mechanism that selects a status
  ladder: brainstorm uses unreviewed/completed, todo uses unverified/confirmed,
  and a decision needs proposed/accepted/rejected/superseded/obsolete. A content
  row cannot select a lifecycle. E-908 is precedent — `decision` was a task type
  before the extraction.
- `task_content` named `decision` carries an IMPLEMENTATION decision: a choice
  made while doing one task, which binds nothing beyond it.

Mike's observation is what motivates the split: when decisions were tasks,
agents rarely filed them and instead buried decisions in plans; since the
extraction, agents file them constantly and file the wrong KIND — task
implementation decisions dressed as architecture.

ED-1590 is the worked example, produced during this very discussion. An agent
filed "a destructive sweep runs on a schedule, never from a hook on the
tool-call path" as an architectural record; Mike rejected it as overbroad —
generalising an absolute prohibition from a single sweep — and as prescribing a
mechanism the code already had. With a `decision` content row available it would
have landed on E-2128 where it belonged, and the pressure to inflate it into a
project-wide rule would not have existed.

### A decision is multi-part, and today's shape cannot hold one

Current decisions carry a single description capped at 1024 characters. Writing
ED-1589 and ED-1590 during this session hit that cap three times — at 1704, 1097
and 1053 characters — and each retry compressed rationale out. What survives is a
statement with a `Rejected:` clause jammed onto the end, competing for the same
budget as the statement itself.

Under `task_content` the parts separate naturally: `statement`, `rationale`,
`rejected`, `consequences`, each its own row with its own room. A decision with
parts is also precisely an Agent Folio Format stream, so the agent-output work
and this one converge rather than competing.

### Numbering

The id spaces ALREADY collide and this is verified, not assumed: ED-1587, ED-1589
and ED-1590 all exist as decisions, and E-1587, E-1589 and E-1590 all exist as
unrelated live tasks. The ranges overlap densely across the corpus.

Therefore:

- **One sequence.** Decisions draw task ids. ED- dies as a NAMESPACE; there is no
  separate dispenser. (Note: a single dispenser across all entity kinds was
  considered previously and rejected; this is narrower — it merges decisions into
  tasks only.)
- **A one-time renumber**, with a permanent alias from each legacy ED- id to its
  new task id. Roughly 1,600 rows, closed at the merge, never growing again.
- **No stored epoch.** An epoch constant and an alias lookup are behaviourally
  identical: look the id up, and a miss means it is post-merge and the number IS
  the task id. The boundary is defined by the table's contents rather than by a
  constant somebody has to maintain and can get wrong.

### One prefix for all tasks

ED- does NOT survive as a live display prefix, and the deciding argument is
mutability: `task update --type` exists, so a type-derived prefix changes a
task's display id when the task is retyped — silently invalidating the form of
every reference already written in plans, lessons, briefs and the ledger. That
defect applies to ED- as much as to a hypothetical EF-/EB-/ER-/EE- family, unless
decision-type were immutable by rule.

The type is already present in every output (`type=todo`), so a per-type prefix
carries no information that is otherwise unavailable — it carries it redundantly,
at the cost of being wrong after a retype.

ED- therefore survives only as a legacy alias prefix that resolves, never as a
rendering. The rule becomes: one prefix per TABLE, with no per-type variation
within tasks.

### Renumber the entity, never the references

Do not rewrite content that mentions ED-NNNN. Three reasons, the first decisive:

1. **The ledger cannot be rewritten.** It is write-only by design and holds the
   bulk of the references, so a rewrite could not be complete even in principle —
   it would leave prose rewritten and history not, which is worse than leaving
   both.
2. Prose references live in plans, analyses, LESSONS.md and the private briefs: a
   mass find-and-replace with no rollback, over content whose correctness nobody
   can verify by reading.
3. Resolution is free. ED-1589 hits the alias, resolves, displays. Old documents
   stay true and the lookup absorbs the change.



### The disk mirrors move too, and this epic owns that move

Noted 2026-09-15. E-2137 phase B consolidates task content into
`.endless/tasks/e-NNNN/<type>.md` and explicitly leaves decisions where they
are, at `.endless/decisions/ED-NNNN.md`, on the grounds that `ED-NNNN` has no
owning task and so is not task-scoped.

That reasoning is correct today and stops being correct the moment this epic
lands. Once a decision IS a task, its mirror is task-scoped like every other
task's content and belongs under `.endless/tasks/e-NNNN/`.

**The move belongs here, not in E-2137**, for the same reason Mike left
`decisions.text` alone: a decision's id changes in the renumber, so moving the
files before that means moving each one twice and landing it at a name that is
about to be wrong. Doing it here moves each file once, straight to its final id
and path.

Concretely, this epic's implementation has to:

- Relocate each decision's content from `.endless/decisions/ED-NNNN.md` to the
  merged task's directory, at the new id, not the legacy one.
- Split it into parts if the multi-part shape above is adopted — `statement`,
  `rationale`, `rejected`, `consequences` — rather than carrying one blob.
- Remove `.endless/decisions/` once empty.
- Leave the legacy `ED-NNNN` ids resolving through the alias table. The FILES
  move; the references do not, per the renumber-the-entity-never-the-references
  rule above.



# Evidence from a supersede, 2026-09-23: there is nowhere to put reasoning

A decision today carries a TITLE and a DESCRIPTION and nothing else. The
description is capped at 1024 characters and must be a single line — no
newlines. `decision add` and `decision update` offer `--description` and
`--description-file`; there is no `--analysis`, no `--plan`, no long-form field
of any kind.

The content model has to answer for that, because it bites hardest exactly when
a decision matters most:

- **Retiring a decision has nowhere to merge its reasoning into.** ED-1570
  superseding ED-1567, and ED-1596 superseding ED-1595, each required folding the
  predecessor's surviving rationale into the successor so the retirement lost
  nothing. Both merged texts (1398 and 1669 chars, several paragraphs each)
  were refused. Every attempt was compressed until it fit, and each pass dropped
  something real — the SQLite-nullability sentence from ED-1570, the E-1972
  worktree measurements and the verify-suite citations from ED-1596. Nothing was
  lost permanently only because both brainstorm outcomes (E-1944, E-1972) happen
  to carry the same content at full length.
- **So the durable record is the task outcome, and the decision is a pointer to
  it.** That is the shape in practice. Whether it is the shape intended is this
  brainstorm's question — and if it is, the decision's own field should say so
  rather than being a place people try to write reasoning into and get refused.
- **Single-line is a separate constraint from the cap and hurts more.** A
  1024-character budget is defensible for a blurb; forbidding paragraph breaks
  inside it makes even a well-sized decision unreadable, and rules out any
  structure (the two directions of a version comparison, a list of what a change
  drops).
- **The refusal message points at fields that do not exist.** It reads "Long-form
  goes in --analysis (rationale) or --plan (the plan)" — borrowed from the task
  validator. On a decision it sends the author somewhere there is nothing.

Carrying decisions on tasks would inherit tasks' own content model, where
`analysis` and `plan` already exist and already hold long-form. That is an
argument FOR the move that this analysis did not previously make.

## From the description

Also settle the relation verb for a task bound by a decision — 'implements' is wrong, since a standing rule is never discharged by the task that first satisfies it — along with its inverse, and ensure a task can show the decisions that bind it.

See analysis.

fields.title: Add a way to revert a settled decision to proposed
fields.description: Add verbs that move an accepted or rejected decision back to proposed, one guarded per status plus one that reverts whichever applies, so an accidental accept is no longer permanent.

Before this, 'decision accept' and 'decision reject' were one-way: 'decision update' has no --status flag and no reverse verb existed, so an accidental accept was permanent.

Immediate need: ED-1517 was accidentally accepted and must be reverted so it can then be rejected or superseded per E-1863.
fields.analysis:
Ships three verbs: 'decision unaccept' (accepted to proposed, guarded on 'accepted'), 'decision unreject' (rejected to proposed, guarded on 'rejected', and clears the stored rejection_reason), and 'decision reconsider' (dispatches to whichever applies, unguarded).

Deliberately NOT named 'reopen': a decision is proposed and then accepted or rejected, so it is never 'open'. The guarded pair is the primary surface because each verb asserts the status you believe you are in, so aiming one at the wrong terminal status errors instead of silently performing the other reversal.

fields.title: Add task unsettled to explain why a worktree is unsettled
fields.description: Add endless task unsettled, listing each task whose worktree is unsettled with a one-line reason, or for one task a breakdown of its modified files and unlanded commits.
fields.context:
The flat `session status` view marks a row unsettled with a bare ◆ but never says why, and the two sub-states need opposite fixes (modified means commit-or-discard, unlanded means land), so the user must run git by hand in the worktree to find out

-- E-1537's worktree is the case that prompted this.
fields.analysis:
## Naming

`unsettled`, not `unlanded`. ED-1540 defines unsettled as the union (modified OR
unlanded); `unlanded` names only one of the two sub-states and would be actively
wrong for a worktree that is unsettled purely because of uncommitted changes.
Under `task` (4 chars) as requested, and it pairs with the existing `task landed`.

## The predicate already exists -- explain it, don't reimplement it

`taskWorktreeDirty` (internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go) is what drives the ◆:

  1. `git -C <wt> status --porcelain` non-empty            -> modified
  2. else `git -C <wt> rev-list main..HEAD --count` > 0    -> unlanded
  3. no worktree, or any git error                         -> settled (fail-open)

It considers neither remote state nor the `task_landings` rows. The new command
must report these exact signals so the marker and its explanation cannot
disagree. Build it as a diagnostic over that predicate, not a second copy.

`AnnotateSessionStatusDirty` (reap_worktrees.go) is the fan-out; the reaper
inverts the same two signals at reap_worktrees.go ("never reap unsettled").

## Reuse

- `internal/monitor/worktree_anomalies.go` -- finer-grained probes
  (`WorktreeAnomaliesAt`, line 91) already split user dirt from auto-managed via
  `AutoManagedStatusGlobs` (line 37). Read `.endless/plans/E-1758.md` before
  touching the anomaly core.
- `src/endless/worktree_cmd.py` `_git_status_partition` -- returns
  (auto_commit_files, user_work_files); the Python mirror of the same split.
- `src/endless/worktree_cmd.py` `_guard_dirty_worktree` -- land-time refusal
  with separate messages for auto-managed vs user dirt; same message shapes apply.

## Where the code goes

- Register in `src/endless/cli.py` immediately after `task_landed` (~line 1393),
  same decorator set (`item_id` optional TASK_ID, --project/--all/--limit/--llm/
  --json) and the same lazy `from endless.task_cmd import ...` inside the body.
- Implement `unsettled_list` / `unsettled_item` in `src/endless/task_cmd.py`
  alongside `landed_list` (line 1551) / `landed_item` (line 1635); mirror its
  three output modes (json / llm / human table).

## Sequencing risk

E-1825 ("Replace union-sense 'dirty' with 'unsettled'") is `unverified` and
renames exactly these identifiers across exactly these files. Either sequence
this after E-1825 lands or expect to touch the same symbols.

## From the description

bare form lists every task whose worktree is unsettled with a one-line reason each; with an ID, print the full breakdown (which files are modified, auto-managed vs user work; how many commits ahead of main and which). Support --llm and --json.

Named `unsettled` not `unlanded` because ED-1540 defines unsettled as the union (modified OR unlanded), so `unlanded` would name only one sub-state.
